info.title: Quizzivy API
info.description:
The contract both the React SPA and the Go backend implement.

**This file supersedes spec §15**, which documented an assumed surface.
Where they differ, this file wins and the spec gets corrected (§18).

Everything else is generated from here: `oapi-codegen` produces the Go
server interfaces, `openapi-typescript` produces the TS types, and MSW
fixtures are validated against these schemas. CI regenerates and fails on
drift. Change the contract here first, then `make gen`.

Non-upload request bodies are capped at 1 MiB before schema validation;
oversized bodies receive HTTP 413 with the standard validation-error envelope.
A body the server could not finish reading receives HTTP 408 with
`REQUEST_INCOMPLETE`.
Multipart media uploads retain their separate upload limits.

## Reading this file

- Operations with `security: []` are **public**. Spec §6.5 requires every
  one of them to be rate-limited; the server asserts this at startup by
  cross-referencing this file, so adding a public operation without a
  limiter fails the process rather than shipping.
- Paths are split by audience: `/teacher/*` is the teaching workspace,
  `/admin/*` the Admin console, `/app/*` the student app, and `/auth/*`
  the caller's own session. `/public/*` and `/join/*` hold open operations
  only, and `/me/*` holds the caller's own notifications and settings,
  whatever their role. Each
  tree accepts only the permissions that belong to it, and the server
  refuses to start when an operation's `x-permission` does not fit its
  tree.
- Every operation that requires a bearer token declares the permission it
  needs in `x-permission`, in one of three forms:
  - a `PermissionKey`;
  - a pseudo-key: `self` (any signed-in user), `workspace.teacher` (any
    `content.*`, `teaching.*` or `people.students.*` key) or
    `workspace.admin` (`people.users.manage`, `people.roles.manage`,
    `system.audit.read`, `system.settings.write` or `scope.all`);
  - a list, met by any one of its keys. A list is used only where one
    operation serves two matrix rows, and the server narrows the check
    when the body decides which row applies.

  An operation that does not require the bearer token (the nine open
  operations) declares none. The server refuses to start when an
  operation breaks this, and a hidden key (`scope.all`,
  `system.api_reference`, `system.data_export`, `system.leads`) may appear
  only under `/admin/`.
- Every uuid-typed path, query or body field under `/teacher/*`, `/app/*`
  and `/me/*`, and every key of a body map whose `propertyNames` is
  `Uuid`, is named in its operation's `x-resource` list as
  `{in, name, kind}`. For a body field `name` is a JSON pointer, where `-`
  stands for every item of an array, `*` for every value of a map and `+`
  for every key of a map.
  `kind` is the owned resource the id names: `test`, `test-version`,
  `section`, `question`, `version-question`, `version-recording`,
  `question-group`, `media`, `import`, `import-source`, `class`,
  `assignment`, `attempt`, `student`, `notification` or `override`. The two `version-` kinds are a
  question and a group recording of a published version, as grading and
  the student's autosave, events and plays name them. A section unit's
  `id` names a question or a group, as its `kind` says, and is declared
  as a question; the suite checks the group branch separately.
  `kind` is `none` for an id that names no owned resource: an option, a
  gap, a session, an idempotency key, a fresh identity the caller
  supplies, a cursor that only marks a position in the caller's own list
  (`before` on `listNotifications`), or an id the operation resolves only
  inside the resource its path names, such as a group's own members on
  `updateQuestionGroup`.
  An `override` is named by the id of the student it is on, beside the
  assignment in the same path: `DELETE /teacher/assignments/{id}/student-overrides/{studentId}`.
  Every `/teacher/*` list names the kind it lists in `x-resource-list`.
  The two-teacher isolation suite reads both: another owner's id answers
  exactly as a missing id does.
- Student-facing schemas are deliberately separate components from teacher
  ones. See `StudentQuestion` for why.
- All timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC. Rendering in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` is the
  client's job (§13.2).
- During a maintenance window every operation except `GET /livez`,
  `GET /healthz` and `GET /public/status` answers `503 MAINTENANCE`
  (`components/responses/Maintenance`). The operations the client branches
  on declare it; every other one may answer it all the same.

tags.name: public
tags.description:
Unauthenticated. Rate-limited per §6.5, and every response is leak-reviewed:
no class, student or test is enumerable through them.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, Google sign-in with PKCE, the rotating refresh token, password change and the caller's own sessions.

tags.name: teacher-tests
tags.description: Tests, their drafts and sections, shared-context groups, publishing, versions and the preview.

tags.name: teacher-questions
tags.description: The question bank, with its tags, its search and the question groups it holds.

tags.name: teacher-imports
tags.description: Private Word source intake and durable import review.

tags.name: teacher-media
tags.description: The media library, its images and audio, their names and where they are used.

tags.name: teacher-assignments
tags.description: Giving a published version to classes and students, its schedule and rules, overrides and results.

tags.name: teacher-ai
tags.description:
The AI assistant's suggestions and the teacher's own credits. Every
operation answers a suggestion or a figure and never writes a grade, a
question or a comment: a teacher accepts a suggestion through the
existing write. With no provider configured every one answers
`501 AI_OFF`.

tags.name: admin-users
tags.description: The Admin console's people operations. In R2 only the deletion of a student account lives here.

tags.name: admin-roles
tags.description:
Roles and the permission matrix. A role is created and edited, never
deleted (DG-52). Every write is held to the subset rule: a caller acts
only on a role whose permissions, except `learning.take_tests`, are their
own, and grants only keys they hold. The built-in roles keep their key.

tags.name: admin-ai
tags.description:
The AI credits console: the pool, the teachers' allowances, their
requests for more and the centre's rules. With no provider configured
every operation answers `501 AI_OFF`.

tags.name: admin-docs
tags.description: Admin access to the API reference served beside the API.

tags.name: admin-audit
tags.description:
The Admin console's audit log: a read-only history of the sensitive
changes the server recorded, filterable by category, search and date, and
downloadable. Nothing here can change or remove an entry.

tags.name: admin-exports
tags.description:
The full data export. The worker builds one ZIP of CSV files, the
requester is told by email, and the file is fetched from an app page up
to three times: the email links to that page and never to the file. Without
object storage and the worker every operation answers `501 EXPORT_OFF`.

tags.name: admin-overview
tags.description:
The Admin console's Overview, its sidebar badge and the Plan & usage
figures: read models over what the other parts of the system hold. Each
section a caller's keys do not open is `null`, so a custom role reads
only what it may.

tags.name: admin-settings
tags.description:
The centre's own settings: who it is and how it is reached, its logos,
how people sign in, and how long it keeps answers, focus events and
disabled accounts. One document for the whole installation.

tags.name: student
tags.description: The student console, with its classes, assigned tests, results and settings.

tags.name: take-test
tags.description: Taking a test, from starting or resuming an attempt to saving answers, submitting and the integrity beacon.

tags.name: me
tags.description:
The caller's own notifications and notification switches, for any
signed-in user. Every operation reads and writes the caller's rows only:
none takes a user id, and none answers 403 or 404 for an id.

bearerAuth.description:
~15 minute access token, held in memory only — never `localStorage`,
never `sessionStorage` (§5.2). On 401 the client calls `/auth/refresh`
once and retries; a second 401 logs out.

refreshCookie.name: quizzivy_refresh
refreshCookie.description:
Opaque, rotating, `httpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/auth`, and
host-only — no `Domain` attribute, so only the API host receives it.
`SameSite=Lax` is sufficient because the SPA and the API are subdomains
of one registrable domain and are therefore same-site.

Presenting an already-rotated token revokes the whole family (§5.2).

Page.name: page
Page.description:
1-based page number. Lists are OFFSET-paginated so a client can draw
numbered pages (O-20 overrides §13.8's keyset rule for the teacher's
lists: at this scale the teacher wants "trang 3 / 26" more than
stability under concurrent inserts). A page past the end is an empty
`items` with the same `total`.

Page size is `limit`, declared per operation with its own default -- a
media grid wants a different page from a table of tests. The response
echoes the size actually used as `pageSize`; compute page counts from
that and `total`, never from an assumed size.

Query.name: q
Query.description: Free-text search. Accent-insensitive (D-11) — `phat am` matches `phát âm`.

BadRequest.description:
Request validation answers this on every operation that takes a JSON body,
before the operation runs: a body that fails its schema, that cannot be
decoded, or that is not JSON.
Malformed or failing validation. A JSON body in which an object repeats
a member name is refused here too, at any depth, unless the server
filled a default into that body: it is then read with the last
occurrence of each repeated name.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired access token. Client refreshes once, then logs out.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated but not permitted: the caller's role lacks the operation's
`x-permission`, as a `student` reaching a `/teacher/*` route does. It
gets this, and the client renders a 403 page rather than redirecting —
a redirect hides the misconfiguration (§5.4).

NotFound.description: No such resource, or the caller may not know it exists.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the caller may retry.

Maintenance.description:
`MAINTENANCE` — a maintenance window is under way. `details.startsAt` and
`details.endsAt` name it, and `Retry-After` is the seconds until it ends.
Any operation except `GET /livez`, `GET /healthz` and `GET /public/status`
may answer this, whatever its authentication.

AiOff.description:
`AI_OFF` — the AI assistant is not configured on this server (no provider
key). Nothing was reserved or metered. `GET /public/status` says `ai: false`.

ExportOff.description:
`EXPORT_OFF` — this server has no object storage or no worker, so it
builds no export. Nothing was queued.

AiNotAllowed.description:
`AI_PAUSED` — an Admin paused AI for this teacher; nothing was reserved.
`AI_READ_OFF` — the teacher's `ai.readStudentAnswers` preference is off,
and the operation would send a student's answer (`suggestAiScore`,
`explainAssignmentResults`). `FORBIDDEN` — `suggestAiScore` and
`explainAssignmentResults` also need `teaching.grading`.

AiCreditsExhausted.description:
`AI_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED` — the teacher's allowance or the centre's pool
cannot cover the call. `details.scope` is `teacher` or `pool`. Nothing
was written, and no call was made to the provider.

AiUnavailable.description:
`AI_UNAVAILABLE` — the provider timed out, was overloaded, refused, or
answered something the server could not use. The reservation was
settled for what the provider billed, if anything, and released
otherwise. A later attempt may succeed.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the caller may try again.

ContentDocument.description:
Versioned learner content, independent of editor JSON. This additive contract
is not yet accepted by question writes. Validate with the content domain
validator as well as JSON Schema: unique gaps, rectangular non-overlapping
table spans, no nested tables, list-leading paragraphs, unordered start=1,
no simultaneous super/subscript, consistent asset kinds, Unicode scalar strings
without NUL, and aggregate budgets. Unknown fields are errors, never silently stripped.
Asset IDs are references only; authorization, existence, kind and deletion
locks belong to the enclosing write. This schema grants no asset access.

href.description: Explicit HTTPS navigation with ASCII DNS-style host labels and optional port 1–65535. International hosts must be punycoded; IPv6 literals are not supported in this version. No credentials, whitespace, controls, backslashes or malformed percent escapes. Never fetched during parsing or rendering.

Uuid.description: uuidv7 — time-ordered, so `id DESC` is a valid recency sort (§13.2).

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC. Rendered in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` by the client.

Points.description:
numeric(8,2) — never a float (§13.2). Stored and compared as an exact
decimal server-side; this is the wire representation.

`format: double` is load-bearing rather than decoration. Without it
oapi-codegen generates `float32`, which holds about 7 significant
decimal digits — and the maximum below needs 8. `999999.99` round-trips
through a float32 as `1000000`, a value this very schema rejects, and
`12345.67` becomes `12345.669921875`. Points are summed to produce a
test's total, so that error accumulates across a paper. `double` gives
Go a float64 and leaves TypeScript's `number` unchanged, since a JS
number is already a float64.

maintenance.description: The next maintenance window that has not ended, or `null`.

ai.description:
Whether the AI assistant is configured. It reads the server's
configuration and never asks the provider, so it says nothing about
the provider being reachable. When false every `/teacher/ai/*` and
`/admin/ai/*` operation answers `501 AI_OFF`, and the web draws no
AI entry point.

PublicOrganization.description:
What `GET /public/organization` answers: the lines the front door prints
about the centre, its logos and the ways in it offers. A line the centre
has not filled is `null`, and the front door then prints its build value.

lightUrl.description:
The light logo's path on the API's origin, carrying its content
hash as `v`, so a new logo is a new URL and the bytes behind one
never change; `null` when the centre has none.

darkUrl.description: The dark logo's path, as `lightUrl`; `null` when the centre has none.

password.description: Whether email and password sign-in is offered.

joinCodes.description: Whether students can join a class with a code.

OrganizationLogo.description: A stored logo, named by the SHA-256 of its bytes.

OrganizationProfile.description:
Who the centre is and how it is reached. Every text is trimmed; an
optional one that is empty after trimming is stored as `null`.

website.description: A domain or an `https` address, without spaces or credentials, as `quizzivy.com` or `https://quizzivy.com/lien-he`. `http` and other schemes are refused.

contactEmail.description: An address of a local part and a domain with a dot, as `hello@quizzivy.com`.

light.description: The logo on a light background, or `null` for none.

dark.description: The logo on a dark background, or `null` for none.

SignInPolicy.description: How people sign in. At least one of `google` and `password` is on.

forcePasswordChange.description: Whether a temporary password issued from now on must be changed at the first sign-in. Passwords issued before keep what they had.

joinCodes.description: Whether students can join a class with a code.

allowedGoogleDomains.description:
The email domains a Google account must be in to sign in, link or
join; empty allows every domain. Stored lower-case.

RetentionPolicy.description:
How long the centre keeps what it collects. The nightly sweep applies
it once enabled (T-R5.17a); `null` means for ever, or never.

keepAnswersMonths.description: Months an answer is kept after its attempt ends, or `null` for ever.

anonymiseDisabledAfterMonths.description: Months after which a disabled account is anonymised, or `null` for never.

OrganizationSettings.description: The whole settings document, as stored.

revision.description: Grows by one with every save; a save names the revision it was read at.

updatedBy.description: Who saved last, or `null` before the first save and once that account is gone.

OrganizationSettingsInput.description: The whole document to store, and the revision it was read at.

SignInImpact.description:
What a proposed policy would do to the active accounts. A method counts
for an account when the policy allows it: a password when the account
has one, Google when a linked Google account's email is in an allowed
domain (any domain when the list is empty).

affectedUsers.description: Active accounts left with no method that counts.

affectedAdmins.description: Of those, the accounts of the built-in Admin role.

actorLocked.description: Whether the caller is among them.

lockout.description: Whether a save would be refused with `SIGN_IN_POLICY_LOCKOUT`; the caller is locked out, or no active built-in Admin keeps a method.

OrganizationLogoUpload.description: A logo stored and ready to be named in a save.

active.description: True while the window is under way.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable, machine-readable. **The only thing clients branch on.** Copy is
driven by `message`, never reconstructed from this, with two exceptions
the web app words itself, as the design deck draws them:
`INVALID_CREDENTIALS` on the sign-in page and `PASSWORD_UNCHANGED` on
the change-password forms. The server still sends a localised `message`
for both, for any other client.

Two codes answer requests this contract does not describe, with this
envelope: `NOT_FOUND` (404) for a path outside it, and
`METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` (405, with an `Allow` header) for a path of it
under a method the path does not serve. `HEAD` is served as `GET`
without a body on the operations that need no token.

`REQUEST_INCOMPLETE` (408) answers a request whose body the server
could not finish reading, on any operation that takes a body other than
a streamed upload. It says nothing about the body: the same request may
be sent again.

ErrorDetail.description:
Extracted so a response carrying the envelope AND something else can
reference it without composing over a closed schema (issue #41).

message.description:
Copy for the user, written by the server in the language
`Accept-Language` prefers: Vietnamese by default, including when
the header is absent or names neither language, and English when
it prefers English. Display it; do not build copy from `code`,
except for the two codes the `ErrorCode` description names.

details.description:
Shape depends on `code`. Field-level validation errors land here
as `{ field: message }` for react-hook-form.

The per-field sentences the rules word for a refused question,
test or assignment, and the `message` of each publish violation
they produce (every one but that of a test with no part at all),
are Vietnamese whatever the header says (issue 284). A per-field
sentence the operation words itself follows the header, as
`message` does.

requestId.description: The copyable error ID shown by the global error boundary (§9).

PageInfo.description:
The paging half of every list envelope. `total` counts the rows that
match the CURRENT filters -- the number the page count is drawn from
-- and is present even on an empty page past the end.

WordImport.description:
Belongs to the teacher who created it (`createdBy`). `scope.all` reaches
any import by id; the history (`listWordImports`) holds only the
caller's own.
Sources are private originals, never learner media. Source revision zero
means no completed source set. Upload completion does not mean recognition.
Pending uploads are durable reservations and cannot be downloaded or processed.

draftRevision.description: Zero until processing has produced a reviewable draft.

testId.description: The draft test created by commit.

filesRemovedAt.description:
When retention removed this import's original files and review draft.
Set only on committed or cancelled imports. Afterwards the history row
and source metadata remain, but downloads, the source view and the
review answer 410 IMPORT_FILES_REMOVED.

closedIdle.description:
Present and true when retention closed this import because nobody
touched it for the idle period, rather than a teacher cancelling it.

readWithAi.description: Whether the files are read with the AI assistant. Absent means false.

WordImportHistoryItem.description:
History-only current draft counts; unknown for a draft untouched since deploy.
Belongs to the teacher who created it (`createdBy`). `scope.all` reaches
any import by id; the history (`listWordImports`) holds only the
caller's own.
Sources are private originals, never learner media. Source revision zero
means no completed source set. Upload completion does not mean recognition.
Pending uploads are durable reservations and cannot be downloaded or processed.

draftRevision.description: Zero until processing has produced a reviewable draft.

testId.description: The draft test created by commit.

filesRemovedAt.description:
When retention removed this import's original files and review draft.
Set only on committed or cancelled imports. Afterwards the history row
and source metadata remain, but downloads, the source view and the
review answer 410 IMPORT_FILES_REMOVED.

closedIdle.description:
Present and true when retention closed this import because nobody
touched it for the idle period, rather than a teacher cancelling it.

readWithAi.description: Whether the files are read with the AI assistant. Absent means false.

ImportReviewCounts.description: Findings from the current review body, never a pending reprocessing candidate.

ImportStatusFacets.description: Counts under the same search and caller-owned scope, ignoring the status filter.

processing.description: awaiting_sources, queued, processing and committing together.

ImportRun.description: The latest processing run. errorCode names why a failed run stopped; keyPaper is the answer-key paper the teacher chose for it, absent when recognition picked one.

requestId.description: Scoped to the actor; replay with the same title returns the same import, changed title conflicts.

readWithAi.description:
Read the files with the AI assistant, so a scanned or photographed
PDF is read instead of refused. Absent means false. When it is true
the pages of the files are sent to an AI service outside Quizzivy.

includeAnswers.description: Whether the ZIP also holds `answers.csv`, every answer of every attempt.

DataExport.description:
One data export. `status` is `queued` until the worker claims it,
`running` while it builds the file, `ready` once the file is stored and
the requester has been told, `failed` when it could not be built (the
requester may ask again), and `expired` once the 24 hours of a `ready`
export have passed. `downloadedAt` is the first time the file was
fetched, and `downloads` counts how many times a URL was handed out (0
to 3): the third fetch is the last. `bytes`, `completedAt` and
`expiresAt` are `null` until the export is ready.

intakeEnabled.description:
Private import storage is configured, so imports can be created,
listed, reviewed and committed. When false, every other
/teacher/imports operation answers 501.

processingEnabled.description:
A worker is deployed to process the queue, so processWordImport
accepts work. When false it answers 503
IMPORT_PROCESSING_UNAVAILABLE instead of queueing a run nothing will
claim. Never true while intakeEnabled is false.

ImportRetention.description:
How long an import keeps its original files and review draft. After
the test is created, after cancellation, and an import untouched for
idleDays is closed and its files removed. History rows are kept.

formats.description: Accepted file extensions; doc appears only when legacy conversion is enabled.

requestId.description: Replaying the same request returns the same run.

keyPaper.description: Paper number to read from an answer-key file that holds several papers.

requestId.description: Replaying a committed request returns the same test.

ImportSourceRef.description: Unicode code point range of one extracted source block.

ImportDraftAnswer.description:
unknown means the source has no key; it is never a set of false options.
Choice keys are optionIds, a short answer's sample is text, fill-blank
keys live on blanks. conflict keeps every source value in candidates.

ImportDraftQuestion.description: unsupported marks content no interaction can represent; it must be retyped or excluded.

ImportGapLink.description: Binds a passage gap to a choice question, or to one blank of a fill-blank question.

ImportDraftGroup.description: Questions sharing one passage; the passage gaps bind to members by stable IDs.

ImportDraftItem.description: Exactly one of question or group.

ImportDraft.description: The reviewable exam. Notices are source observations and are kept by the server; edits never change them.

ImportReview.description:
The draft with every current finding. ready is true only when nothing blocks
and every review_required finding has a decision. reprocessed means a newer
machine draft exists that has not replaced the teacher's edits.

ImportSourceView.description: The extracted main-body text of one source, in document order, for side-by-side review.

PermissionKey.description:
The permission catalogue, in the order of the Roles & permissions
matrix, and equal to the rows of `app.permissions`. Each key and the
matrix row it is:

- `content.tests.write`: Create and edit tests
- `content.tests.publish`: Publish tests
- `content.questions.write`: Manage question bank
- `content.media.write`: Upload and delete media
- `content.share`: Share own content with other teachers
- `ai.use`: Use AI features
- `teaching.classes.write`: Create classes
- `teaching.assignments.write`: Assign tests to classes
- `teaching.grading`: Grade answers
- `teaching.attempts.intervene`: Reset, void or extend attempts
- `teaching.attendance`: Take attendance
- `people.students.read`: See students in own classes
- `people.students.create`: Create student accounts
- `people.students.reset_password`: Reset student passwords
- `people.users.manage`: Add and disable users
- `people.roles.manage`: Change roles
- `system.audit.read`: View audit log
- `system.settings.write`: Change system settings
- `learning.take_tests`: Take tests and view own results
- `ai.credits.manage`: Manage AI credits

`ai.use` gates every `/teacher/ai/*` operation and the import's "Read
with AI"; `ai.credits.manage` gates every `/admin/ai/*` operation. The
Admin holds both, the built-in Teacher holds `ai.use`, and a custom role
may hold either alone. `ai.credits.manage` opens no workspace by itself.

The last four keys in the enum are hidden: no matrix row shows them,
no role is granted them, and only the Admin holds them. The Admin
holds every key, and `learning.take_tests` only when that cell is
turned on. `scope.all` reads and edits any teacher's content, classes
and people by id, and widens the lists of classes, students and
attempts and the dashboard's figures to every teacher's. It does not
widen the teaching workspace's six content lists: `listTests`,
`listQuestions`, `listQuestionGroups`, `listMedia`, `listWordImports`
and `listAssignments`, with their facets, tags and counts, hold the
caller's own rows for every caller (for assignments, those the caller
created and those that target a class the caller teaches).

RoleIcon.description: The Edit role dialog's twelve icons; the same set `app.roles.icon` checks.

RoleColor.description: The Edit role dialog's seven card colours; the same set `app.roles.color` checks.

BuiltinRoleKey.description: The immutable key of a built-in role. A custom role has none.

custom.description: True when the role is not built in.

userCount.description: Accounts that hold the role, disabled ones included.

permissions.description:
What the role's users may do, in catalogue order, without the
hidden keys: the matrix column. The Admin's is every matrix key
except `learning.take_tests`, which it holds only when that cell
is turned on.

revision.description: Moves with every change to the role. Sent back as `expectedRevision` so a stale save is refused.

editable.description:
False where the subset rule stops the caller from acting on the
role: it holds a permission the caller lacks, `learning.take_tests`
apart. The caller's own role is editable here, but its permissions
are never changed by its holder (`CANNOT_ACT_ON_SELF`).

inProgressAttempts.description: Attempts in progress right now by users who hold the role.

adminLocked.description: True where the Admin's cell cannot be changed, which is every key but `learning.take_tests`.

roles.description: Every role, in the order Admin, Teacher, Assistant, Student, then custom roles oldest first.

catalogue.description: The matrix rows in order. The hidden keys are left out.

studentTarget.description: True for the built-in Student and any custom role whose permissions are a subset of `learning.take_tests`, so a custom role with no permission at all is a student target.

name.description: At most 60 characters after Unicode NFC.

description.description: At most 300 characters after Unicode NFC.

copyFromRoleId.description: The role whose permissions the new role starts with. Omitted, it starts with none.

name.description: At most 60 characters after Unicode NFC.

description.description: At most 300 characters after Unicode NFC.

expectedRevisions.description: The revision of every role a change touches, as the matrix last read it.

roles.description: The roles the save touched, as they stand after it.

AccountStatus.description:
The one state an account is listed under (DG-54), in this order of
precedence: `disabled`, then `must_change_password` (a temporary
password is still in use), then `never_signed_in` (`last_sign_in_at` is
null), then `active`.

hasPassword.description: false for Google-only accounts. Gates the unlink affordance.

mustChangePassword.description: Forces `/change-password`. Always false for Google-only users (§5.4).

UserPreferences.description: Stored account preferences; omitted keys use client defaults without materializing them.

ai.description:
The AI assistant's preferences. Like `assignmentDefaults`, the object
is replaced whole by a merge, and an omitted key uses the client's
default: the language of the interface, tags on, reading student
answers on, reading imports off. The server reads
`readStudentAnswers` before an operation sends a student's answer.

tagDrafts.description: Tag what the assistant writes as an AI draft until a teacher edits or approves it.

readStudentAnswers.description: Let the assistant read student answers, for grading suggestions and results insights. Never a name.

readImports.description: Read scanned and unusual imports with the assistant.

Workspace.description:
A console the signed-in user may enter: `teacher` for any `content.*`,
`teaching.*` or `people.students.*` permission; `admin` for
`people.users.manage`, `people.roles.manage`, `system.audit.read`,
`system.settings.write` or `scope.all`; `app` for
`learning.take_tests`.

CurrentUser.description:
The signed-in user, as only the user sees it: `User`'s properties plus
the permissions the user's role holds, in catalogue order, and the
workspaces they open. Written flat, because a closed schema cannot be
extended with `allOf` (issue #41). `User` stays where a response
describes someone else, so a student's permissions never reach a
teacher's payload.

avatarUrl.description:
The caller's profile photo as a presigned `GET`, valid 24 hours and
minted again on every response that carries it. Absent when the
caller has no photo. Set and cleared by `setAvatar` and
`deleteAvatar`.

hasPassword.description: false for Google-only accounts. Gates the unlink affordance.

mustChangePassword.description: Forces `/change-password`. Always false for Google-only users (§5.4).

passwordChangedAt.description:
When the caller last changed their own password. Absent for an
account that never has, including one still on a temporary password
and one whose password is older than R5. Self only: it is on
`CurrentUser` and not on `User` or `StudentRow`.

GoogleSignInSuccess.description:
AuthSuccess plus the class a join code enrolled the student in.

Flat rather than `allOf: [AuthSuccess, ...]`: AuthSuccess is
`additionalProperties: false`, and in JSON Schema 2020-12 that keyword
cannot see a sibling allOf branch, so the composed form rejects the very
body it documents (issue #41).

enrolledClass.description: Present only when a `joinCode` produced an enrolment.

PublishConflict.description:
The publish 409: the error envelope plus every blocking violation, so the
builder marks them all inline rather than surfacing one per attempt (§8).
Flat for the same reason as GoogleSignInSuccess.

GradingQueue.description: Complete filtered pending counts with a deterministic prefix of at most 200 saved answers.

groups.description: Only groups represented in items, in queue order; remaining counts each group's complete filtered work.

studentsWaiting.description: Distinct student UUIDs across all filtered eligible answers.

key.description: Canonical lowercase student UUID, or assignmentUUID:versionQuestionUUID in question mode.

label.description: Raw current student full name or decimal paper question number for client localization.

sub.description: Live assignment title of this group's first returned item.

remaining.description: Complete filtered eligible answer count; may exceed the returned prefix for this group.

GradingQueueItem.description: One saved pending-manual answer and its frozen teacher question; identity is attemptId plus questionId.

studentName.description: Raw current full name, without private account fields.

questionNumber.description: One-based section/question paper order, independent of the student's shuffle.

score.description: Manual score; null while this answer remains in the pending queue.

QuestionAnswerRow.description: One paper's answer to the question G-04 is grading.

answer.description: Null when the student left it blank, which cannot be marked.

ReferencingTest.description:
A test that holds a reference the caller asked to remove, named so a
blocked delete can say where to look instead of only that it is
blocked (A-06a, A-07).

version.description:
The published version holding the reference. Absent when the
reference is a draft outline, which has no version yet.

ReferencingGroup.description: Teacher-only shared context that protects an immutable media asset, including archived bank groups.

testId.description: Owning test, absent for an independent bank group.

ReferencedBy.description:
What still references a row whose permanent delete answered
`RESOURCE_REFERENCED`, carried as `details.referencedBy` by
`deleteClass` and `deleteUser`. `other` is a reference the server does
not name. Later releases add values; a client treats an unknown one as
`other`.

previous.description:
The old file, which has left the library, and what keeps it in
storage. A server always sends it; a client reads its absence as a
server from before files were kept for the tests that use them.

repointed.description: Distinct live question rows and groups actually changed; question rows differ from LibraryAsset.questionCount's derived usage.

left.description: Other owners' live question rows and groups still using the old asset; excludes versions, import reviews and late same-owner bindings.

MediaRetirement.description:
A file that has left the library, because `replaceMedia` replaced it or
`deleteMedia` deleted it, and what keeps it in storage. The file stays
readable for as long as anything uses it, and in its owner's quota
(`MediaUsage.heldBytes`). Seven days after nothing uses it, it is
removed from storage for good and cannot be restored, so `url` is the
teacher's chance to download it.

url.description: Short-lived signed URL of the old file (§11.2).

usedIn.description:
The published test versions that still use the file, one entry per
version, as `LibraryAsset.usedIn` lists them; a client counts the
distinct test `id`s for "used by N published tests". Always empty
after `deleteMedia`, which refuses a file a version uses.

deleteAt.description:
When the file is removed from storage, if nothing uses it now: seven
days from now. `null` while a published version, or content of
another owner, still uses it; the removal is then seven days after
the last of them stops, and that time is not known yet.

LibraryAsset.description:
A MediaAsset as the teacher's media library lists it: with the name the
library shows, its default play limit, an image's size in pixels, how
many questions use the file and how many published versions reference
it. Flat for the same reason (issue #41) -- this is
the site that was actually shipping a body its own contract rejected.

displayName.description:
The name the library shows: the one `updateMedia` stored, or
`originalFilename` while none was set.

defaultMaxPlays.description:
The default play limit stored with this audio, for a client to
start a question's own limit from when it attaches the file; the
server applies it to nothing. `0` is unlimited and `null` is not
set. Always `null` for an image.

width.description:
An image's width in pixels. `null` for audio, and for an image
whose header could not be read; `width` and `height` are `null`
together.

height.description: An image's height in pixels; `null` exactly when `width` is.

questionCount.description:
How many questions use the file, each counted once: a question
that is not deleted and attaches it, and every member that is not
deleted of a question group whose recordings or materials hold it.
Any owner's questions count. A published version, and a group with
no member, add nothing here; `usageCount` counts versions.

usedIn.description:
The published tests behind `usageCount`, one entry per version,
so the blocked-delete dialog can name them (A-07).

MediaFacets.description:
How many files of the caller's library each tab holds for the CURRENT
search, ignoring the `kind` and `unused` filters themselves, so that
choosing a tab does not zero the others. `unused` counts the files
whose `questionCount` is zero.

MediaUsage.description:
What the caller's library holds, beside the quota an upload is
measured against. `audioBytes` and `imageBytes` are the files in the
library, whatever the search and the filters.

A file that was replaced or deleted leaves those two figures but not
the quota while anything still uses it: a published test version, or
content of another owner. `heldBytes` is those files, and the quota
check counts `audioBytes + imageBytes + heldBytes`.

Seven days after nothing uses a replaced or deleted file it is removed
from storage for good. `pendingBytes` is the files waiting for that and
`pendingDeleteAt` the earliest time one of them goes. They count toward
neither the quota nor the figures above; they are for information.

A server always sends `heldBytes`, `pendingBytes` and `pendingDeleteAt`.
They are not required so that a client built for this contract still
reads a server from before files were kept for the tests that use them,
where a missing figure means none held and none pending.

quotaBytes.description: The most one owner's library may hold, as the deployment sets it.

heldBytes.description:
Replaced or deleted files that published test versions, or content
of another owner, still use. They count toward the quota until
nothing uses them.

pendingBytes.description:
Replaced or deleted files that nothing uses any more and that wait
seven days for removal. They do not count toward the quota.

pendingDeleteAt.description:
The earliest time one of the files in `pendingBytes` is removed
from storage; `null` or absent when none waits.

MediaUpdate.description:
What `updateMedia` changes. A property left out keeps its stored
value.

displayName.description: Trimmed by the server; a name that is blank once trimmed is refused.

defaultMaxPlays.description:
`0` is unlimited and `null` clears the limit. A number is refused
for an image.

StudentAssignmentDetail.description:
The intro screen's card: what StudentAssignmentCard carries, without
`classId`, `classIds` and `liveAnsweredCount`, plus the policies §10.2 states in
plain Vietnamese before the student starts. The window it states is the
student's own, as in StudentAssignmentCard.

review.description:
On the intro's detail these are the stored flags, and `release` says
when they apply; they become effective only on the student's result.

studentNote.description: The teacher's note for the students, plain text. Null or absent when there is none.

hasAudio.description: Any question audio or shared recording on the assigned frozen version.

hasSharedAudio.description: A shared recording has one allowance across its group's questions; absent means false for legacy readers.

showsTranscript.description: True when any question audio or shared recording releases its transcript after submitting.

audioMaxPlays.description: The strictest finite `maxPlays` across question audio and shared recordings on the assigned version; null when all are unlimited. Individual recordings can have higher limits.

StudentClass.description: A class the student is in, with how they got there (§6.4's D-10).

StudentActivity.description:
Backs G-07's "Hoạt động" column, which has three renderings and needs
two facts to pick between them: "đang làm bài" while an attempt is live,
a relative time when there is a last one, and an em dash when the student
has never started anything.

`live` is not `lastAttemptAt is recent`. Nothing in this system flips an
attempt when its deadline passes -- assignment status is derived for
exactly that reason (D-18) -- so a stale in-progress row would read as
"đang làm bài" forever. The server ANDs the status with `deadline_at`.

live.description: An attempt is in progress and inside its deadline.

StudentStats.description:
Per-student teaching figures for §8's students table (G-07) and the class
roster (G-06), over only the assignments the caller reaches: those they
created and those targeting a class they teach, or every one with
`scope.all`.

Deliberately NOT on `User`. `User` is the `/auth/me`, `/auth/login` and
`/auth/refresh` payload, so a field added there is shipped to the student
about themselves on every cold load and every token refresh. §13.5's
student-projection guard would not catch it either -- it sweeps `/app/*`
and `/auth/me` is not one.

submittedCount.description:
Distinct ASSIGNMENTS with at least one attempt that reached the
teacher, not attempts. With `maxAttempts > 1` the two differ, and
counting attempts would print "14" beside an average taken over 7
things.

score.description:
Weighted: the sum of earned points over the sum of available points,
across each assignment's best graded attempt. Sent as the pair rather
than a percentage because every other score in this contract is an
(earned, total) pair, and the client can render either reading.

Null when nothing is graded yet, which is G-07's "—". An unsubmitted
assignment is never a zero: "chưa nộp" and "—" are different facts,
and collapsing them is how a gradebook lies.

StudentRow.description:
One row of §8's students table. Flat rather than `allOf: [User, ...]`:
`User` is `additionalProperties: false`, and in JSON Schema 2020-12 that
keyword cannot see a sibling `allOf` branch, so the composed form
rejects the very body it documents (see issue #41).

disabledAt.description:
Set means the account cannot sign in. Present on the row because
`updateStudent` accepts `disabled: false` in both directions, and a
state that can be written but never read is a one-way door: the
student would vanish from every listing with nothing able to name
them again.

lastActiveAt.description:
The student's latest authenticated request, which the server records
at most once every five minutes per instance (DG-54). Null before
the student has ever been active. Not the same as
`stats.activity.lastAttemptAt`, the last time they started a test.

classes.description: Memberships in classes the caller teaches, or every one with `scope.all`. The table truncates; the drawer lists them.

StudentPasswordReset.description: One student `resetStudentsPasswords` reset. The password is shown once.

StudentResetFailure.description: One student `resetStudentsPasswords` did not reset, and why.

StudentFacets.description:
G-07's "31 học viên · 23 hoạt động 7 ngày qua". Counts a page
cannot express, in the same shape as TestStatusFacets. Both count only
the students the caller reaches, and `activeLast7Days` only work on
assignments the caller reaches.

`active` reuses the dashboard's window verbatim rather than defining a
second meaning of active on a second screen.

accessToken.description: Held in memory only (§5.2). The refresh token is set as a cookie, not returned here.

SetPasswordLinkInfo.description:
What a valid set-password link is for: the account it controls, which
the page names so a person can tell the link is theirs, and when it
stops working. The email and the name are the account's own, given to
whoever already holds the secret that controls it.

purpose.description: `invite` for a new account's first password, `reset` for a new one.

Session.description:
One sign-in of the caller that is still live: a refresh-token family
that is neither revoked nor expired (§5.2). It is the caller's own and
nobody else's. It carries no IP address, no raw user agent and nothing
that could be presented as a credential.

`device` is computed from the user agent when the list is read and is
made only of names from a closed list, "Mac · Chrome", "Mac" or
"Chrome", never of any part of the header itself. It is null, and
`deviceKind` is `unknown`, when neither the system nor the browser is
recognised; the client words that case in the reader's language.
`deviceKind` picks the icon. An iPad that asks for desktop sites sends
a Mac user agent and reads as one.

`location` is "City, CC", the place of the request that last signed in
or refreshed this session, taken from the edge's location headers and
only where the server trusts them. It is null otherwise. `lastUsedAt`
is that same moment, so it is at most one access-token lifetime old.

current.description:
True for the session the request's refresh cookie belongs to. False
for every session when the request carries no cookie that names a
live session of the caller.

scheduleLabel.description: When the class meets, as its teacher worded it ("Thứ 3, 5 · 18:00"). Plain text, trimmed; `null` for none.

room.description: Where the class meets. Plain text, trimmed; `null` for none.

openAssignmentCount.description: Assignments whose derived status is `open` and that target this class (G-08).

archivedAt.description: Set once archived. An archived class leaves every picker and keeps its record (G-08).

joinCode.description: Teacher responses only. Never present on a `/app/*` response.

averageScore.description:
Teacher responses only. Never present on a `/app/*` response: a student
does not see how the class did. The sum of earned points over the sum of
total points of the best graded attempt (the highest score, the later
attempt on a tie) of each **current member** on each assignment that
targets the class, with the manual answers still unmarked in those
attempts as `pendingManual`. A student who has left the class counts for
nothing. Voided attempts and attempts not yet graded are ignored. `null`
when nothing is graded yet.

ClassListItem.description:
A row of `listClasses`: every property of `Class`, with `joinCode` read in
full. It repeats `Class` rather than extending it so that no other
operation's response carries a readable code; a test holds the two property
lists together. `joinCode.code` is the code when the request asked for codes
with `withCodes`, the caller holds `teaching.classes.write`, and
`getJoinCode` would read that class's code for that caller; otherwise it is
`null`.

scheduleLabel.description: When the class meets, as its teacher worded it ("Thứ 3, 5 · 18:00"). Plain text, trimmed; `null` for none.

room.description: Where the class meets. Plain text, trimmed; `null` for none.

openAssignmentCount.description: Assignments whose derived status is `open` and that target this class (G-08).

archivedAt.description: Set once archived. An archived class leaves every picker and keeps its record (G-08).

joinCode.description: The active code with its metadata, or `null` for a class with none. Teacher responses only.

averageScore.description: As `Class.averageScore`; `null` when nothing is graded yet.

JoinCodeInfo.description:
Metadata about the active code — **not the code itself**, which
`getJoinCode` reads for its teacher. A code issued from v0.8.0 on
is stored encrypted under a key the database does not hold and found
by a keyed hash (§13.3), so a database dump does not hand it over. A
code issued before v0.8.0 is held only as its SHA-256 hash, which a
dump can reverse beside the hint, until it is rotated (D5).

JoinCode.description:
A class's active join code, read back for its teacher (D5), with the
metadata `JoinCodeInfo` carries.

code.description: Grouped `XXXX-XXXX`, or `null` when the code cannot be read back.

legacy.description: True for a code issued before v0.8.0, held only as a hash until it is rotated.

ClassFacets.description: G-08's tab counts for the current search, ignoring the status filter; `students` are distinct live members.

stats.description: The same figures G-07 shows, so G-06's roster carries "Bài đã nộp" and "Điểm TB".

joinedVia.description: Lets the teacher spot unexpected enrolments (§6.4).

joinCodeHint.description:
Which code this member used, if any. After a rotation this
distinguishes "joined via the code that leaked" from "joined via the
current one" (D-10).

MyClass.description:
A class as its student sees it (S-10): the name, who teaches it, when
and where it meets, and when they joined. Never the join code, a count,
the roster or an average.

teacherName.description: The display name of the class's own teacher.

teacherAvatarUrl.description: The teacher's profile photo, a presigned GET valid 24 hours; `null` when the teacher has none or no store is configured.

scheduleLabel.description: When the class meets, as its teacher worded it.

MediaAsset.description:
A stored file as a question, a preview and a student's paper carry it.
`x-media-limits` is what an upload may be (§11.1): audio of at most
`audioBytes` and `durationMs`, an image of at most `imageBytes`. The
server's constants and the web's pre-check are tested against it.

url.description:
Short-lived signed URL, 10 minutes (§11.2). Treat as expiring: on a
403, refetch rather than failing. Hiding this URL is not protection
and no further investment is planned.

bytes.description: At most `audioBytes` for audio, and `imageBytes` for an image.

durationMs.description: Audio only, and always present for audio. Probed server-side (§11.1).

AudioPolicy.description:
Present if and only if the attached asset is audio (§7). This is the
authoring shape, read and written by teachers; a student receives
`StudentAudioPolicy`.

maxPlays.description:
`null` is unlimited. Enforcement is server-side and advisory: over-limit
plays are reported to the teacher, never blocked or retroactively
penalised (§11.4).

allowPause.description:
Whether a student may pause the recording once it is playing (§11.1);
`true` when none was ever set. The server always sends it. In a request
an absent field means "do not change it": a create stores `true`, and an
update keeps the value already stored for the same question (by its id),
for the same member question of a group (by its id in the bundle) and for
the same recording (by its id). An audio policy or a recording that is new
in the request is a create. A client that does not know the field therefore
can never switch pausing back on by saving.

StudentAudioPolicy.description:
The audio rules a student's engine reads, for a question's audio and for a
group's recording. The shape of `AudioPolicy` with every field required,
because the engine never guesses a rule the server did not send. These are
rules the student is meant to read; nothing here is an answer key.

allowPause.description: Whether the student may pause the recording once it is playing (§11.1).

QuestionContent.description:
Bounded semantic prose for prompts and explanations: paragraphs, headings,
lists and tables with marked text, breaks and safe links. No media, gaps,
source metadata or answer-key properties. ContentDocument aggregate budgets
and cross-node validation apply to original raw JSON. The companion string
must equal the exact plain projection. Explanations never contain gaps.
On question updates, omitting a rich field preserves its stored document
only if the companion string is unchanged; otherwise the whole write is
rejected. Explicit null removes the document.

QuestionPromptContent.description:
Bounded semantic question prompt without media or answer keys. Gaps are
supported only for fill_blank and must match blank gapId values exactly.
Gap identity is stable within this question; labels never select answers.
The companion prompt equals the exact plain projection. Omitted content
on update preserves the stored document only when prompt is unchanged.

OptionContent.description:
Versioned inline option text: one paragraph of marked text and line breaks.
No links, gaps, media, tables, source metadata or answer keys. The server
validates the original JSON and requires text to equal its plain projection.
Omitted content preserves rich formatting only when the current option id and
text match; stale or changed legacy writes are rejected. Explicit null
removes formatting. Options without rich content remain plain text.

gapId.description: Stable identity of the rich prompt gap; null for legacy Markdown.

ordinal.description: Stable 1-indexed answer label; matches `{{1}}` only for legacy Markdown.

AuditCategory.description:
The six families of the audit log's tabs. An entry about the
organization, an export, maintenance, retention or the AI credits is in
none of them.

AuditCategoryFacets.description:
How many entries each category holds for the CURRENT search and range,
ignoring the category filter itself, in the shape of `TestStatusFacets`.
`all` counts every such entry, including those in no category.

avatarUrl.description: A signed address for the actor's photo. Absent when they have none.

type.description: The kind of thing, as the server stores it (`class`, `test`, `media_asset`, `word_import`, ...).

id.description: `null` for an entry about no single row.

label.description:
The name of the user, class, test, assignment, attempt (its
student), media file, import or question group, read when the page
is read. `null` when the row is gone or has no name.

from.description: The value before the change. Any JSON value, `null` included.

to.description: The value after the change. Any JSON value, `null` included.

actor.description: Who did it; `null` is the system itself, or an account since removed.

action.description:
A stable key such as `class.created`. The sentence that words it is
the client's, from `audit.action.<action>`; an action a client has
no sentence for is shown humanised.

category.description: `null` for an entry only the unfiltered list holds.

ip.description: The address the request came from. `null` for the system.

device.description: A label such as `Mac · Chrome`, classified from the user agent; `null` when none was recorded or none is recognised.

details.description: Whatever the entry recorded beyond `changes`; `null` when nothing.

ApiReferenceSummary.description:
What `getApiReferenceSummary` reports about the embedded contract.
`endpointCount` is the number of operations, and a group's `count` the
number of operations that carry its tag.

openapi.description: The OpenAPI version the contract is written in.

AdminOverview.description:
The Admin console's Overview. A section the caller's keys do not open
is `null`; `attention` is then shorter, never an error.

organizationName.description: The centre's name, from its organization settings.

attention.description: What needs doing, most urgent first. Empty when nothing does.

recentChanges.description: The five newest audit entries of any category, newest first. Needs `system.audit.read`.

AdminOverviewPeople.description:
The accounts of the centre. A student is a student target of R2's
student-like roles and a teacher is every other account, an Admin and
a custom role included. `teachers` are the enabled ones and
`teachersDisabled` the disabled ones, so the two never overlap. `total`
and `students` count disabled accounts, as the Users tabs count them.

activeThisWeek.description: Accounts with an authenticated request on any of the last seven local days, today included, whether they have been disabled since or not.

teachersDisabled.description: Disabled accounts that are not a student target; none of them is in `teachers`.

studentsNewThisMonth.description: Students whose account was created since the first of this local month.

AdminDailyActive.description:
Who made an authenticated request on each of the last fourteen local
days. Staff is every account that is not a student target, which the
chart labels Teachers. A day counts the accounts that were active on it,
whether they have been disabled since or not.

days.description: One entry per day, oldest first and today last, zero days included.

average.description: The mean of students plus staff over the fourteen days, rounded half up.

AdminAttention.description:
One thing that needs doing. `count` is at least 1: a row with nothing
to do is not sent.

count.description:
`must_change_password`: enabled accounts on a temporary password.
`never_signed_in`: enabled accounts that have never signed in and
are not on a temporary password. `disabled_teacher_classes`: classes,
archived ones too, whose teacher is disabled. `storage`: how many of
the media and import meters with a configured limit read 80 percent
or more, as `detail` quotes them (rounded half up). `ai_credit_requests`: the teachers waiting for more credits
this month.

detail.description: What the row's line quotes. `null` for `must_change_password`.

AdminAttentionDetail.description:
The facts a row quotes, by kind; a field its kind does not use is
absent. `never_signed_in`: `oldestCreatedAt`.
`disabled_teacher_classes`: `className` and `teacherName` of the newest
such class. `storage`: `mediaPercent` and `importsPercent`, each absent
when that meter has no limit. `ai_credit_requests`: `teacherName`,
`used` and `allowance` of the request waiting longest.

mustChangePassword.description: Enabled accounts on a temporary password; `null` without `people.users.manage`.

Usage.description:
What the centre uses against its plan. Nothing is enforced (DG-55): a
`limit` is `null` when its `PLAN_*` variable is unset, and a figure may
pass its limit.

`seats` counts the accounts that are not disabled against
`PLAN_SEAT_LIMIT`. `teachers` counts the enabled accounts that are not
a student target, Admins included, against `PLAN_TEACHER_LIMIT`; it is
the Overview's `people.teachers`. `media` is the bytes of the media
files still held in storage, against `PLAN_MEDIA_BYTES`, and `imports`
the bytes of the source documents of
the imports whose files are still kept and the number of those imports,
against `PLAN_IMPORT_BYTES`. `attemptsKept` has no limit until a
denominator is named.

aiCredits.description: The month's credits. `null` without `ai.credits.manage`, and while the AI assistant is off.

TestStatusFacets.description:
How many tests each status holds for the CURRENT search, ignoring the
status filter itself — selecting one tab must not zero the others.
Backs A-03's "Tất cả 12 · Bản nháp 3 · Đã phát hành 8".

AssignmentStatusFacets.description:
How many assignments each derived status holds right now, ignoring
the status filter itself, so the list's tabs carry counts the way
A-03's do.

QuestionTypeFacets.description:
How many questions each type holds for the CURRENT tag and search,
ignoring the type filter itself. Backs A-06's rail counts.

prompt.description:
Legacy Markdown, or exact plain projection when promptContent is present. Markdown is rendered with rehype-sanitize — never
`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (§2). For `fill_blank`, blanks are marked
`{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, 1-indexed, matching `blanks[].ordinal`.

mediaAlt.description: The alt text a teacher wrote for the question's image; absent or null when there is none, and always when `media` is not an image.

sampleAnswer.description:
`short_answer` only. **Teacher-only, shown during grading.** Never
appears in any `/app/*` schema, including the result endpoint.

usedInTests.description:
How many DRAFT test outlines reference this question. Editing the
bank copy changes every one of them, which is a versioning event the
teacher deserves to know about before they type (A-06). Published
versions are deliberately not counted: they hold their own snapshot
and a bank edit cannot reach them (§7).

usedIn.description: Current test outlines using the question, sorted by title. Included on individual question responses; loaded on demand for the bank's nested usage table. Published snapshots are excluded.

StudentOption.description: No `isCorrect`. Deliberately not a subset-by-omission of AdminQuestionOption.

StudentBlank.description:
No `acceptedAnswers` — that is the grading key. `caseSensitive` is a
rule, not a key: the engine states it under the blanks (S-05, "Không
phân biệt hoa thường"), and a rule the student cannot read is one they
are graded on blind.

gapId.description: Stable identity of the rich prompt gap; null for legacy Markdown.

StudentSection.description:
One part of the paper, in test order. `instructions` is the teacher's
text to the student for this part; the engine shows it above each of the
section's questions and the navigator groups the numbers under
`title` (S-05, S-06, S-08).

StudentQuestion.description:
What a student receives while taking a test. Contains none of
`isCorrect`, `sampleAnswer`, `acceptedAnswers`, `transcript` — asserted
by a contract test over this file and by an E2E test over a live
response (§14 E2E 9).

Options arrive in the order the student must see them, already shuffled
server-side from the attempt's `shuffleSeed` so a reload cannot reorder
them (D-02).

id.description: A `test_version_questions` id — never a bank question id (§7).

sectionId.description: The `AttemptSession.sections` entry this question belongs to.

mediaAlt.description: The alt text frozen with the version for the question's image, for a screen reader. Absent when the question has none or its media is not an image. It is a description, not an answer key.

StudentGroup.description:
Frozen shared context with ordered version-question identities. Contains
no answer keys or transcripts. Assets are explicitly authorized by the
containing preview/session, never by an arbitrary content assetId.

StudentGroupRecording.description: One versioned group playback scope, independent of other groups using the same file.

SharedReviewContext.description:
Frozen material for completed-attempt results and teacher grading.
Learner transcripts contain only recordings whose own policy releases
them after submission; teacher grading includes all available transcripts.
No grading key is added to groups. Listening here never consumes a play.

transcripts.description: Released transcript text keyed by frozen recording ID; suppressed entries are absent.

audioPlays.description: Used plays by recording for a single attempt; omitted when grading across attempts.

ResultQuestion.description:
The post-submission view. Every revealing field is gated by the
assignment's review policy and simply absent when the policy is off —
the client has no fallback that could surface a suppressed value.

sectionId.description: The part of the paper this question belongs to, one of the result's `sections`. Present under every review policy: the paper already showed the student which part a question was in.

mediaAlt.description: The alt text frozen with the version for the question's image, as on `StudentQuestion`. Present under every review policy: the picture was already on the paper.

answer.description: What the student submitted. `null` if unanswered.

earned.description: Present only when `review.showScore`. `null` while awaiting manual grading.

correctOptionIds.description:
Only when `review.showCorrectAnswers`. Replaces per-option
`isCorrect` so that key name never appears under `/app/*`.

answer.description:
**One canonical accepted answer**, not the full accepted list.
Showing every accepted spelling would hand over the grading key.

explanationContent.description: Absent unless review.showExplanations permits the frozen explanation.

transcript.description:
Only when the question's `showTranscriptAfterSubmit` is on, and only
on this endpoint — never on `GET /app/attempts/{id}` (§13.5). Also
serves as the accessibility fallback for hard-of-hearing students (§11.3).

QuestionGroup.description:
Independent shared-context draft graph, written through the group endpoints.
Array order defines member/material order. Empty draft groups are allowed;
publication requires a member. Members belong to one group in one section.
Copy with context creates fresh group, member, material, gap and recording
identities. Immutable asset bytes may be reused through protected bindings.
Validate graph references and aggregate limits in addition to JSON Schema.
The byte budget includes resolved question content/keys; a transport must
also bound original input before decoding. This is a teacher authoring
shape, never a learner payload or an asset access grant.

optionOrder.description: Fixed is for choice members whose text depends on authored option labels and forbids option shuffling; other members use shuffle. Neither changes member order.

gaps.description: Exactly one binding per material gap; targets must be distinct within the group and refer to its members.

GroupQuestionGap.description: A material gap targets a choice member; display labels never determine identity.

GroupBlankGap.description: A material gap targets the stable prompt gap of a rich fill-blank member, never a mutable answer-row ID.

GroupRecording.description:
Teacher-only authoring shape. One explicit playback binding per audio asset
used in the group's materials. All member questions share its allowance;
another group using the same asset has a different binding. Transcripts
require a separate policy-gated review projection, never a learner cast.

testUpdatedAt.description: Enclosing test revision for section-owned groups; absent for bank groups.

assets.description: Authorized media referenced by members or shared materials.

unavailableAssetIds.description: Bound assets whose metadata or signed link could not be loaded. A media outage does not turn a committed edit into an ambiguous save failure; clients show a retryable material state.

expectedTestUpdatedAt.description: Required when ownerSectionId identifies a section; no ownerSectionId means an independent bank group.
Required for a section-owned group; owner cannot change through this operation.
Required when copying into a section; omitted destination creates an independent bank group.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: The test revision the move was drawn from, as `updateTest` takes it.

questionId.description: A standalone unit's question or a member of a group a section of this test owns.

expectedGroupRevisions.description:
The revision of every group the move touches, once each: the
question's group when it is a member, the destination group when
`to.groupId` is set, and one entry when both are the same group.
A move always touches at least one group.

groupId.description: Null places the question as a unit of the section; set places it as a member of that group, which the section must own.

index.description: Position the question takes among the section's units when `groupId` is null, among the group's members otherwise, counted once it has left its old place, so the same value places it whether it moves up or down. Past the end is clamped to the end.

test.description: The saved draft, with its new `updatedAt` and the sections' units.

questionId.description: The id the question has now. A new id after a copy into a group; the original bank question's id when `restored` is true; the request's otherwise.

copied.description: True when the question was copied into a group and the bank question stays where it was. The builder says so after the drop.

restored.description: True when a member that was an unedited copy of a bank question left its group and the original bank question took its place in the section, the copy being removed. `questionId` is then the original's id.

editedCopy.description: True when a member that was a copy of a bank question which is still in the bank left its group edited, and so stayed a new bank question of its own. False for every other move out of a group, including a member that was never a copy or whose original is gone. The builder says so after the drop.

groups.description: Every touched group at its new revision, built as `getQuestionGroup` builds one.

id.description: Standalone question ID or owned group ID, according to kind.

questionIds.description: Legacy standalone references; group members belong to their group and are excluded here.

units.description: Complete mixed order when the section has shared groups; absent on historical standalone outlines.

TestAssignmentCounts.description:
The assignments that name any version of a test, by derived status
(`AssignmentStatus`), whoever created them. `live` counts the `open`
ones. Drafts are not counted. Backs the tests card's "2 live".

currentVersion.description: 0 while never published. A `published` test always has ≥ 1.

nextVersion.description:
Read-only: the server computes it and a client never sends it. The
number the next publish of this test will take: one more than
the highest version ever published, whether or not that version
still exists, so it is 1 for a test never published. Deleting the
newest version does not lower it, and the publish and this field
read the same count. It is not `currentVersion + 1` and not the
highest listed version + 1, and a client that names the version
about to be published reads it from here.

audioCount.description: Draft questions with their own audio or a shared group recording, counted once per question. Backs A-03's headphone badge.

skills.description: Sorted distinct non-null skills of the current draft, including grouped members.

unpublishedChanges.description:
How many changes the draft holds against the test's latest version:
the length of `getTestVersionDiff`'s `changes` for that version
against `draft`, so 0 means the draft is the latest version. It is
what the unpublished-changes banner reads.

Only `getTest` computes it. It is null for a test with no version,
in every row of `listTests`, in the answer of a write, and when a
group of the draft or of the latest version cannot be read; the
page then shows no banner. A
bank edit to a question the draft uses counts, though it never
moves `updatedAt`.

sections.description: The **draft** outline. Published content lives in versions.

TestVersion.description: Immutable. Editing a published test creates a new one; in-flight attempts keep theirs (§7).

skills.description:
Sorted distinct non-null skills of the questions this version froze,
grouped members included: the version's counterpart of `Test.skills`.
It is read from the version's own questions, so editing the draft or
the bank after the publish does not change it.

audioCount.description: Questions with their own audio or a shared group recording, counted once per question; shown when picking a version to assign (G-01).

manualCount.description:
Questions needing manual grading. G-01 multiplies it by the roster to
show the teacher what they are committing to marking before they
commit to it.

assignmentCount.description:
Every assignment that names this version, drafts included, whoever
created it. A version with one cannot be deleted, so this is what
"In use · {n} assignments" and the disabled Delete read.

changeNote.description: The note the teacher left when publishing. Null for a version published without one.

testUpdatedAt.description:
`publishTest` only: the test's `updatedAt` after the publish, which
the publish itself moves. A caller that goes on saving the draft
sends it as `expectedUpdatedAt`, or its next save answers
`STALE_WRITE`. Absent from every other answer.

DiffSide.description: One of the two papers a diff compares.

version.description: The server sends it exactly when `kind` is `version`. The schema does not tie the two together.

publishedAt.description: The server sends it exactly when `kind` is `version`. The schema does not tie the two together.

DiffChangeKind.description:
What one change reports. A question is never reported twice under one
kind. An edit to the shared material of a group, or to a section,
reaches each of its questions as one `changed` entry (field `context`
or `section`), so `Test.unpublishedChanges` counts it once per
question.

| Kind | The question | `params` |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | in `to` only; `questionNumber` and `questionId` are its place in `to` | `prompt` |
| `removed` | in `from` only; `questionNumber` and `questionId` are its place in `from` | `prompt` |
| `changed` | in both; `questionNumber` and `questionId` are its place in `to` | `fields` |
| `answer` | in both, with a different answer key; its place in `to` | `answerFrom`, `answerTo` for a choice question; none otherwise |
| `points` | none: the test's total changed; no `questionNumber`, no `questionId` | `pointsFrom`, `pointsTo` |

A question that changed in its words and in its key is reported twice,
once as `changed` and once as `answer`. Moving a question to another
place in the paper is not a change.

DiffField.description:
The part of a question that differs, for a `changed` entry.
`prompt` and `explanation` cover the text and the rich content;
`options` the text and content of the choices in their order, `blanks`
the gaps and their case rule, and `media` the attachment with its audio
policy and transcript. `context` is the shared material of the group
the question belongs to, or its being in a group at all, and `section`
the part of the paper it sits in. The correct options and the accepted
answers are not here: they are `answer` entries.

DiffChangeParams.description:
One closed set of fields for every kind; `DiffChangeKind` says which of
them a kind carries. Plain values only.

prompt.description: The question's prompt as plain text, cut to 200 characters with `…` in place of the rest.

answerFrom.description: The labels (`A`, `B`, …) of the correct options in `from`, in order.

answerTo.description: The labels of the correct options in `to`, in order.

questionNumber.description: The question's number in its paper, counting across sections.

questionId.description:
The question's id in the paper `questionNumber` counts in: the
frozen question of a version, the bank question of the draft. It is
the id the preview of that version carries.

TestVersionDiff.description: What differs between two papers of one test.

from.description:
The older paper. Null only for `against=previous` on the first
version, which has nothing before it: every question is then an
`added` one.

changes.description:
Ordered by kind (`added`, `removed`, `changed`, `answer`, `points`)
and then by question number.

PublishValidationError.description:
Publish returns **every** problem at once, each anchored to a question,
so the builder can mark them inline rather than surfacing one per attempt.

AssignmentStatus.description:
**Derived**, never stored (D-18). A pure function of `publishedAt`,
`opensAt`, `closesAt` and an optional early `closedAt`, so it cannot go
stale and needs no scheduler.

`draft` is what an unpublished assignment reads as. It does not weaken
D-18: publishing is an explicit act by the teacher, not a timestamp
arriving, so nothing has to flip a row on a schedule. A draft is
invisible to students and counts towards nothing.

ReviewRelease.description:
When a student's result is released. `on_submit` is as soon as they
hand in. `after_close` is once the assignment has closed for them, at
its effective close: until then the result withholds the score, the
marks, the answer key and the explanations through the same path a
policy that hides them takes, and carries `releasesAt`.

ReviewPolicy.description:
What the assignment lets a student see, as the server reads it. On the
student's result the three flags are the **effective** ones: all three
read false while an `after_close` release has not come, whatever the
teacher chose.

showClassAverage.description:
Whether the result may carry `classAverage`. It says what the
teacher chose; whether the average is there is `classAverage`.

ReviewPolicyInput.description:
The review policy a teacher writes. `release` and `showClassAverage`
are optional: a create without them gets `on_submit` and false, and a
PATCH without them keeps what is stored.

IntegrityPolicy.description:
Defaults are §10.3's, conservative on purpose — the teacher opts into
stricter modes per test. Whatever is enabled is stated in plain
Vietnamese on the intro page before the student starts (§10.2).

maxFocusLoss.description: -1 = no away episodes allowed; 0 = unlimited; positive values = allowed counted episodes.

onLimitExceeded.description: `auto_submit` immediately submits after the allowed number of counted away episodes is exceeded, preserving answers and recording the violation.

minAwayMs.description:
An away episode shorter than this is not a strike. A 2-second blur is
a notification; a 90-second blur is a search (§10.1).

classes.description: The classes this assignment targets, with their names and live member counts.

students.description: The students targeted by name, with their names (G-09's chips).

publishedAt.description: Null while the assignment is a draft.

closedAt.description: Set when closed early by the teacher.

durationMinutes.description:
Server-enforced. An attempt's deadline is
`min(startedAt + duration, closesAt)`, so starting late does not buy
a full duration and does not cut the student off mid-window (O-05).

studentNote.description: The note for the students, as stored. Null when there is none.

submittedCount.description: Distinct enabled students with at least one handed-in non-voided attempt.

questionCount.description: Questions on the pinned version, counted as `TestVersion.questionCount` counts them.

pendingManualCount.description: Outstanding manual answers across handed-in attempts, including partially graded papers.

pendingGradingCount.description: Handed-in attempts with a manual answer still unmarked (G-09's "Chờ chấm").

classIds.description: The classes the copy is assigned to. May be empty, since the copy is a draft and is given its targets later.

handedIn.description:
