The papers the figures range over: for each student the caller
reaches, their latest handed-in attempt that is not voided.

items.description: Sorted by `correctRate` ascending, a question with none last, then by `number`.

number.description: The question's place on the paper, counted across sections.

promptExcerpt.description: The prompt as plain text with its whitespace collapsed, cut at 140 characters.

answered.description: Papers with an answer that says something to this question.

correctRate.description:
Papers that earned the question's full points, over the papers that
have a mark for it. A question left unanswered counts against it; a
manually marked answer the teacher has not marked yet counts for
neither side. Null when no paper has a mark for it.

AttemptSession.description:
Returned when an attempt is created, resumed or read. Everything the
engine needs to run authoritatively.

remainingAttempts.description: Additional attempts available after this one, excluding voided attempts.

testTitle.description: The engine's header names the paper from 1024px up (S-08).

sections.description: In test order. `questions` never interleaves two sections, whatever the shuffle.

questions.description:
Already in presentation order, shuffled server-side and stable
across reloads (D-02). Shuffling happens inside each section, so
the order of sections is the order of `sections`.

groups.description:
Frozen shared context for this attempt's version. Member IDs name
questions in this session; presentation order comes from questions.
No answer keys or recording transcripts. Only version-bound assets
reachable through this student's own attempt receive signed URLs.
Empty for historical standalone papers; optional for compatibility.

sessionId.description:
Identifies this device/tab. Every write carries it; a superseded
session gets `SESSION_SUPERSEDED`, which is how the first tab learns
it lost (§10.1, E2E 7).

beaconToken.description:
Opaque, valid until `deadlineAt`, **append-only event access**.
`navigator.sendBeacon` cannot set an `Authorization` header and the
15-minute access token has usually expired by `pagehide`, so the
beacon carries this in its body instead. Grants no read access.

superseded.description:
Present and true only in an answer of `getAttempt` to a tab that
named a session the attempt no longer has. `sessionId` is then the
session that tab named, `beaconToken` is empty, and every write
under that session answers `SESSION_SUPERSEDED`.

audioPlays.description:
Keyed by question id. **Server-authoritative** — the client renders
remaining plays from this, decrements optimistically, and reconciles
on the next fetch. A client-side counter would reset on reload and
make the limit meaningless (§11.4).

groupAudioPlays.description:
Server counts keyed by frozen group recording ID, shared across all
members and sessions of this attempt. Different groups using the same
file have independent counts. Optional for historical clients.

answers.description: Keyed by question id. The base for the resume merge.

playId.description: Stable random ID for one gesture, reused unchanged by retries; unique within the attempt.

kind.description:
Not an enum: an append-only telemetry log reliably gains kinds, and a
newer client must not fail against an older server. Unknown kinds are
stored, not rejected. Known set is §10.1.

clientSeq.description:
The event's offset in milliseconds from the attempt's start, as the
tab that recorded it measured it against the server's clock, and
never below the number after that tab's last one: it increases
**within a tab**. Uniqueness is `(attempt, session, clientSeq)`: an
event that repeats a number its session has used is taken for a
retry and is not stored. A new session may use any number again
(D-01). A client that sends a plain counter is accepted.

durationMs.description:
For paired events (hidden/visible, blur/focus, fullscreen in/out),
computed server-side. `null` on an unpaired trailing event — the
student never came back — which renders open-ended rather than being
dropped (§10.4).

IntegritySummary.description: The §10.4 summary strip. Neutral by construction — counts, not verdicts.

offlineEpisodes.description: Shown distinctly from focus loss — distinguishing bad wifi from cheating matters for fairness (§10.1).

MonitorRow.description: One row per **targeted student**, including those who never started.

answeredCount.description: Questions whose saved answer says something, by the rule of `StudentAssignmentCard.liveAnsweredCount`, against the response's `questionCount` (G-02's progress column).

extendedTo.description: This student's own close, when an override of theirs reaches past the assignment's own: "Extended to …". Absent or null when they have none, or theirs is no later. While it is ahead of `serverTime` the student can still start or carry on, even if the assignment has closed early or its window has ended.

Dashboard.description:
The Teacher dashboard covers the caller's own teaching, including an Admin:
assignments they created or targeting classes they teach, reachable papers on
them, and their classes. Its repository supports scope.all for a future Admin
console, but this operation never requests it. Legacy fields retain their
meaning; T-R4.23 stops reading openAssignments, activeStudents, totalStudents
and recentAttempts, and R5 removes them. Range affects submissions only.

closingSoon.description: Open assignments closing within the next 24 hours.

waitingStudents.description: Distinct students with unmarked manual answers in handed-in papers.

totalStudents.description: Enabled student-like accounts in the classes the caller teaches, for an Admin too; this operation never requests the repository wide scope.

activeStudents.description: Of the enabled student-like members of classes the caller teaches, those who started an attempt in the last seven days on an assignment they reach; an Admin has the same own scope and cannot request the repository wide reading here.

newestFlaggedAttempt.description: Newest started currently flagged reachable paper, ordered by started_at then id descending, from the flagged count statement snapshot; null without grading or intervention permission or a matching paper. Historical, voided and former-roster papers remain eligible.

DashboardTakingNow.description: Distinct students and assignments with reachable in-progress attempts before their deadline.

assignmentId.description: Assignment of the newest started reachable in-progress paper strictly before its deadline at the supplied application clock, ordered by started_at then id descending, from the taking count statement snapshot; null when none qualifies.

DashboardSubmissions.description: Handed-in papers within the chosen calendar range in the actor's zone, including graded papers.

days.description: One entry per day, oldest first and today last, including zero days.

averagePercent.description: Mean graded paper percentage, rounded half up; null when no graded paper has a score.

DashboardToday.description: Published assignment openings and effective closings today in the actor's zone, oldest first.

notSubmitted.description: Distinct enabled reached targets without a submitted, timed-out or graded attempt on this assignment.

DashboardActivity.description: Latest ten activities, newest first; one row per non-voided attempt, plus student-like joins by code into taught classes.

TeacherSummary.description: Cheap nav counts in the caller's own teaching scope, for an Admin too.

liveAssignments.description: Rows the caller's Assignments list shows as open; always a number under the current workspace.teacher gate.

answersToGrade.description: Unmarked manual answers in reachable handed-in papers; null without teaching.grading, when the count is not run.

submittedCount.description: Distinct enabled students who have handed in at least one non-voided attempt.

targetCount.description: Enabled students in the union of class and individual targets, counting only the classes the caller teaches and the students they reach.

StudentAssignmentCard.description:
`status`, `closesAt`, `durationMinutes` and `maxAttempts` are the
signed-in student's own: when a teacher has given this student an
override, they are the later close, the longer time limit and the added
attempts (T-R4.12), and an assignment that closed for everyone else
reads `open` here while the student's close is still ahead. Nothing in
the card says an override exists or why.

className.description: The class this assignment reached the student through. Null unless exactly one targeted class that is not archived contains them.

classId.description: The id behind `className`, so S-17 can count a class's papers. Null when `className` is.

classIds.description: Every class this assignment targets that contains the student and is not archived, so each class card can name its next paper. Empty for a student targeted only by name.

totalPoints.description: What the paper is out of.

lastSubmittedAt.description: When the last attempt was handed in. Null while it is in progress.

liveDeadlineAt.description: The live attempt's deadline. Absent exactly when `hasLiveAttempt` is false.

liveAnsweredCount.description: How many of the live attempt's saved answers say something, by the rule the engine's navigator uses: a choice with an option picked, a true/false with a value, a text that is not blank, a fill-in with every blank filled. An answer that exists only in the browser's draft is not counted. Absent exactly when `hasLiveAttempt` is false.

score.description: Only when the assignment's `review.showScore` is on.

AiLanguage.description:
The language the text a suggestion writes for a person is written in.
The assistant keeps the language of the material it was given for the
content of a question.

AiUsage.description:
What a call cost and what remains, for the panel's footer. `credits` is
what the provider's usage came to, never more than the call's ceiling.

left.description: The least of what remains of the teacher's allowance and of the centre's pool, after the call.

AiGenerateRequest.description:
Exactly one source: `source` (text the teacher pasted), or `testId`
with `stimulusId` (a shared-content passage of the test's draft). The
first 8,000 characters of a source are sent. Nothing about a student is
ever sent.

explanations.description: Write an explanation for each question.

AiGeneratedQuestion.description:
A draft question. For a choice type `options` holds the options in order
and `answerKey` the text of each correct one, exactly as written in
`options`; a true/false question has the options `True` and `False`. For
`fill_blank` the prompt holds `___` for the gap and `answerKey` the
accepted answers; for `short_answer` it holds the sample answer.

explanation.description: Empty when the request did not ask for explanations.

AiCheckKind.description: Wrong or doubtful answers, unclear wording, answers given away, spelling and grammar.

AiFixPayload.description:
What a one-click fix writes, through `updateQuestion`, into the question
it names: `text` replaces the option `optionId` (`option_text`), is added
as an accepted answer of the blank `blankId` (`accepted_answer`), or
becomes the explanation (`explanation`).

AiFix.description:
`kind` is `none` when the fix is advice only; `payload` is then absent.
Otherwise `payload` is present, and names an option or a blank of the
question when the kind needs one.

label.description: The one-click button's label. Absent when `kind` is `none`.

number.description: The question's 1-based place in the draft.

AiVariantKind.description: Reword questions, reorder options, write new wrong options.

AiVariantPayload.description:
What a change writes, through `updateQuestion`, into the same question
of the copy: `prompt` replaces the prompt (`reword`); `optionOrder`
lists every option of the question in its new order (`reorder`);
`optionId` and `text` replace the text of one wrong option (`distract`).

number.description: The question's 1-based place in the draft, which the copy keeps.

why.description: Why a learner might pick it.

comment.description: A comment to the student, for the teacher to keep, change or drop.

AiInsight.description:
`questionNumbers` are the questions the insight is about, by their
place on the paper, and `types` the distinct types of those questions,
for a practice set. A pattern in answers; never a judgement of a student.

basis.description: How many handed-in papers the insights are based on.

AiCleanupCheck.description: Near-duplicate questions, and questions with no tags.

usedInTests.description: Draft outlines that use the question.

AiCleanupResult.description:
Over the caller's own questions only, newest first, at most 2,000 of
them: `scanned` is how many were read, and `truncated` says the bank
held more than that, or more untagged questions than the 200 one
request suggests tags for, or that part of the pass failed or ran out
of time.

AiCreditCategory.description:
The Settings card's rows: generating questions and variants, grading
suggestions, explanations and wrong options, reading imports, and
checks, word lists and insights.

month.description: The first day of the month the request is for.

AiMonthUsage.description:
One teacher's month. `left` is the least of what remains of the
allowance and of the pool, never below zero. `requests` says whether the
centre takes requests for more credits (its rule is to ask, not to
pause); `pending` is the teacher's undecided request this month.

month.description: The first day of the month, counted in the centre's time zone.

categories.description: The five rows of the usage card, in the order it draws them.

poolCredits.description: The plan for a month that has not begun.

defaultAllowance.description: What a teacher without a custom allowance may use in a month.

warnPercent.description: The share of the allowance at which the teacher is told.

onTeacherLimit.description: Pause a teacher who runs out, or let them ask for more.

rewritten.description: How many of this month's allowances the new default rewrote.

AiPool.description: The centre's month. `total` is `plan` plus `added`; `left` counts calls in flight as spent.

AiTeacherMonth.description:
One teacher's month on the Admin page. `allowance` includes `granted`,
the credits approved requests added; `custom` says the allowance was set
for this teacher and a change of the default leaves it.

AiAllowanceInput.description:
Changes how much one teacher may use this month, or pauses or resumes
them. `custom: true` sets the teacher's own allowance to `credits`;
`custom: false` returns them to the default and takes no `credits`.
An omitted field keeps what is stored.

AiPendingRequest.description: A request waiting for an Admin, with the standing of the teacher who made it.

AiAdminCredits.description:
The Admin's view of the current month. `onPace` is the credits the month
is on course to use, `used` over the days elapsed times the days in the
month, and `withinPool` says it fits the pool. `allowances` is the sum
of the teachers' allowances, which may exceed the pool. `active` counts
teachers who used AI this month and `idle` those who hold `ai.use` and
have not.

AiCreditDecision.description:
A request after a decision. `allowance` is the teacher's allowance for
the month after an approval, and zero after a decline.

NotificationKind.description:
What a notification is about. The server sends no sentence: the client
words the item from `kind` and `params` in the reader's language.

Each kind carries exactly these `params`:

| Kind | For | Params |
|---|---|---|
| `attempt.submitted` | a teacher | `title`, `count`, `toGrade` |
| `attempt.flagged` | a teacher | `studentName`, `title`, `focusLost` |
| `assignment.closing` | a teacher | `title`, `notSubmitted` |
| `class.joined` | a teacher | `studentName`, `className` |
| `join_codes.rotated` | a teacher | `count`, `classNames` |
| `assignment.opened` | a student | `title`, `closesAt` |
| `assignment.due_soon` | a student | `title`, `closesAt` |
| `assignment.extended` | a student | `title`, `closesAt` |
| `result.ready` | a student | `title` |
| `ai.allowance_warning` | a teacher | `used`, `allowance` |
| `ai.credit_request` | a teacher | `teacherName`, `credits` |
| `ai.credit_request.decided` | a teacher | `credits`, `decision` |

The three `ai.*` kinds are for the teacher's bell. `ai.credit_request`
is written for every holder of `ai.credits.manage`, who reads it in the
teacher workspace until the Admin console has a bell of its own.

NotificationAudience.description:
The console that reads a notification, and so which of the caller's
notifications a bell counts, lists and clears. Which kinds each one
reads is the "For" column of the table in `NotificationKind`, and every
kind belongs to exactly one.

Where an operation takes it, it is optional, and leaving it out keeps
the behaviour from before it existed: every kind. An Admin who takes
tests holds rows of both, and each of their two bells passes its own.
It only narrows: the rows are still the caller's own and nobody else's.

NotificationEvent.description:
One switch of the notification settings. `attempt.submitted`,
`attempt.flagged` and `assignment.closing` are the teacher's;
`assignment.due_soon` and `result.ready` the student's. A switch
governs the kind of the same name, and `assignment.due_soon` also
governs `assignment.opened` and `assignment.extended`. `class.joined`
and `join_codes.rotated` have no switch.

NotificationParams.description:
What the client builds a notification's sentence from. One closed set
of fields for every kind; `NotificationKind` says which of them a kind
carries. Plain values only: never markup, never a score, a band or an
answer. A name is a copy taken when the notification was written.

title.description: The title of the test the assignment gives.

count.description: Papers handed in (`attempt.submitted`), or classes whose join code was replaced (`join_codes.rotated`).

toGrade.description: Of the papers handed in, those with an answer waiting for a mark.

focusLost.description: Times the student left the test.

notSubmitted.description: Students who have not handed in.

classNames.description: At most five names; `count` holds how many classes there are.

used.description: AI credits the teacher has used this month.

allowance.description: The teacher's AI allowance this month, in credits.

credits.description: AI credits a request asks for.

teacherName.description: The teacher who asked for credits.

decision.description: How an Admin decided a request for credits.

NotificationTarget.description:
Where a click on the notification goes: a page the client resolves from
`route`, never a URL. `assignmentId` is present for `assignment` and
`studentAssignment`, and `attemptId` for `attempt` and `result`; either
may accompany any other route.

route.description:
`assignment`, `attempt`, `grading` and `classes` are pages of the
teaching workspace; `result` and `studentAssignment` are the
student's result and the student's page of an assignment.

target.description: Null when the notification leads nowhere.

readAt.description:
When the caller marked it read; null while it is unread. A
notification that is written again after it was read, as a count
that grew is, is unread again.

inApp.description: While false, no notification this switch governs is written for the caller.

email.description: Stored and returned. Nothing is sent by email yet.

NotificationPreferences.description: Every `NotificationEvent` once. The server answers them in the enum's order.

MySummary.description: What the caller's shell shows before any page is open.

QuestionInput.description:
Create/update body for a bank question. Cross-field rules that a single
schema cannot express — single_choice and true_false need exactly one correct
option (true_false has exactly two options), multiple_choice needs at least one correct
option, a `fill_blank` needs exact gapId bindings for rich prompts or matching
`{{n}}` ordinals for legacy Markdown, an audio policy requires an audio asset and alt text an image — are validated by the
server and again at publish (§8). Failing them returns
`VALIDATION_FAILED` with per-field `details`.

prompt.description: Legacy Markdown, or exact plain projection when promptContent is present. `fill_blank` uses stable gapId bindings in rich content and `{{n}}` placeholders in legacy Markdown.

mediaAlt.description: Alt text for the question's image, for screen readers (1 to 1000 characters). Refused with a field error on `mediaAlt` unless `mediaAssetId` names an image; send null, or omit it, to clear it. A write replaces the stored value, as it does for `level` and `skill`, so an update that leaves it out clears it.

audio.description: Required if and only if the asset is audio (§7).

transcript.description: Audio questions only. Teacher-authored; the student sees it only per policy.

options.description: Order in the array is the stored ordinal.

sampleAnswer.description: `short_answer` only. Rejected on any other type.

StoredQuestionInput.description:
Stored editable content used by teacher reads, bodyless copies and version
restoration. Existing choice arrays retain their length; the eight-option
limit applies to authoring requests. Cross-field rules that a single
schema cannot express — single_choice and true_false need exactly one correct
option (true_false has exactly two options), multiple_choice needs at least one correct
option, a `fill_blank` needs exact gapId bindings for rich prompts or matching
`{{n}}` ordinals for legacy Markdown, an audio policy requires an audio asset and alt text an image — are validated by the
server and again at publish (§8). Failing them returns
`VALIDATION_FAILED` with per-field `details`.

prompt.description: Legacy Markdown, or exact plain projection when promptContent is present. `fill_blank` uses stable gapId bindings in rich content and `{{n}}` placeholders in legacy Markdown.

mediaAlt.description: Alt text for the question's image, as stored. Absent or null when there is none.

audio.description: Required if and only if the asset is audio (§7).

transcript.description: Audio questions only. Teacher-authored; the student sees it only per policy.

options.description: Order in the array is the stored ordinal.

sampleAnswer.description: `short_answer` only. Rejected on any other type.

StudentOverride.description:
What one teacher changed about one student's turn at an assignment.
Teacher-only: nothing here, the reason least of all, reaches the
student's payloads.

closesAt.description: The student's own close. Null when the override leaves the close alone. It never closes the student sooner than the assignment does.

durationMinutes.description: The student's time limit. Null when the assignment's applies.

extendBy.description: Minutes added to each student's current close. Not with `closesAt`.

testVersionId.description: Must be a published version. Immutable once any attempt exists.

shuffleQuestions.description: Shuffle standalone questions and complete groups as units inside each section; preserve member order.

shuffleOptions.description: Rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED on shuffleOptions when the selected version contains a group member with fixed option-label dependencies.

studentNote.description:
A note for the students, drawn on the Test intro. Plain text,
trimmed by the server; an empty one, or one that is blank once
trimmed, is the same as none. The 500 characters are counted before trimming. Omitted,
a create has none and a PATCH keeps the stored note; `null` clears
it.

draft.description:
Save without giving it out — G-01's "Lưu nháp". Saving again with
`false` publishes it, which is what the "Giao bài" button sends.

A draft is the only assignment allowed to have no targets: the point
of saving one is to come back to it.

closeNow.description:
PATCH only; a create ignores it. Sets `closedAt`, closing the
assignment before `closesAt`. It is refused with `400
VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `closeNow` while `window.opensAt` is
still ahead, because an assignment cannot close before it opens,
whatever its status.

post.summary: Look up a class by join code
post.description:
Backs the inline preview on `/join` and `/join/:code`, which exists so
the student sees **which class they are joining** before authenticating.
Never create an account and enrol in one blind tap (§6.2).

Lookup is by a keyed hash of the normalized code, or by its SHA-256 for
a code issued before v0.8.0, compared in constant time. The plaintext
is never stored; a code issued from v0.8.0 on is stored encrypted
(§6.5).

joinCode.description:
Accepted with or without the dash and in any case; normalized
before lookup. The alphabet excludes `0`, `O`, `1` and `I` (§6.1).

200.description:
**Leak review (§6.5).** Exactly three fields. No student names, no
counts, no member list, no assignment titles. `classId` is included
because the confirm step needs an idempotency key for the subsequent
enrolment; it is a uuidv7 that reveals only the class's creation time
and grants nothing on its own.

404.description:
Invalid, expired, exhausted, revoked, or self-join disabled.

**Leak review.** These return distinct `code` values so the client can
show an accurate message, but identical `details` — empty — and no
class-identifying text. A disabled-self-join class is indistinguishable
from a nonexistent one. Nothing here lets a caller enumerate classes.

413.description: The body is over 8 KiB, which the rate limiter's keys read in full.

get.summary: Whether the API is down for maintenance, or soon will be
get.description:
The earliest maintenance window that was not cancelled and has not
ended, or `null`. `active` is true while it is under way. During an
active window every other operation answers `503 MAINTENANCE`, and this
one keeps answering, so the client can tell the student when to come
back.

**Leak review (§6.5).** The answer is identical for every caller and
never depends on a token: two timestamps and a flag. No id, no creator,
no count, no free text. It is served from a snapshot the server
refreshes at most every 30 s, so neither its content nor its timing
says anything about the database.

Cache-Control.description: `public, max-age=30`, the snapshot's own refresh interval.

get.summary: The centre as the front door shows it
get.description:
The centre's name and contact lines, its logos and the ways in the
sign-in page offers, so the front door can print them before anyone
signs in. Served from a snapshot the server refreshes at most every
30 seconds.

**Leak review (§6.5).** The answer is identical for every caller and
never depends on a token. It carries only what the front door already
prints: the centre's own name and contact lines, two logo paths, and
three switches the sign-in and join pages act on. No plan, usage or
count, no person or id, no allowed-domain list, no retention value,
and nothing about when or by whom the settings were saved.

The PNG bytes of the light or the dark logo, served as a download and
never read as another type. A `v` equal to the current logo's hash makes
the answer immutable for a year; any other `v`, or none, is cached for
five minutes. No logo of that variant: 404.

**Leak review (§6.5).** Public bytes the centre chose to show on its
front door, the same for every caller. Nothing names the bucket, the
object key or who uploaded them.

Cache-Control.description: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` when `v` is the current hash, else `public, max-age=300`.

post.summary: Email and password sign-in
post.description:
Teacher-created accounts and staff sign-in (§5.1). Self-signup
requires Google (§6.3); there is no password registration endpoint.

200.description: Signed in. Sets the rotating refresh cookie.

401.description:
**Leak review.** `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` for both an unknown email and
a wrong password, with the same message and comparable timing, so the
endpoint is not a user-enumeration oracle. A disabled account returns
the same thing.

403.description:
`PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_DISABLED` — the centre has turned password
sign-in off. It is decided before the email or the password is
looked at, so every password sign-in gets it alike and it says
nothing about any account.

413.description: The body is over 8 KiB, which the rate limiter's keys read in full.

post.summary: Google sign-in, and the only self-signup path
post.description:
The frontend obtains an **authorization code with PKCE** — not an
implicit ID token — and this endpoint exchanges it server-side. The
client secret never leaves the backend (§5.3).

Resolution order (§5.3 step 4), in full:

1. identity exists → log in
2. verified email matches a user → link identity, log in
3. no match **and** a valid `joinCode` → create account + enrol (§6.3)
4. no match, no join code → `403 ACCOUNT_NOT_PROVISIONED`

An ID token with `email_verified: false` is **rejected outright** — no
link, no create, regardless of `joinCode`. This closes an
account-takeover path and is not negotiable (§5.1).

joinCode.description: Present only when signing in to join a class, after the class preview on `/join` or `/join/:code`. Turns this into a signup.

200.description: Signed in, or signed up and enrolled.

Set-Cookie.description: `quizzivy_refresh=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/auth` — §5.3 step 5. Without it the sign-in has no session.

401.description: Code exchange failed, or `email_verified` was false.

403.description:
`ACCOUNT_NOT_PROVISIONED` — a valid Google identity with no matching
account and no join code. The client explains that a class code is
needed rather than offering a signup form (§5.3).

`ACCOUNT_DISABLED` — the matched account is suspended. Named
explicitly here, unlike at password login: the caller has just
proved to Google that they control this address, so the fact
discloses nothing they could not confirm themselves, and an
unexplained failure would send them to support instead of to the
teacher.

`IDENTITY_ALREADY_LINKED` — the verified email matches an account
that is already linked to a DIFFERENT Google `sub`. Linking a second
one would make "unlink Google" ambiguous, so it is refused (D-08).

`GOOGLE_SIGN_IN_DISABLED` — the centre has turned Google sign-in
off. `GOOGLE_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` — the verified address is outside
the centre's allowed domains. Both are decided for a code that
joins a class as well.

404.description: The supplied `joinCode` was invalid, expired, exhausted or revoked. **No account is created.**

413.description: The body is over 8 KiB, which the rate limiter's keys read in full.

post.summary: Read what a set-password link is for
post.description:
The set-password page calls this with the token it read from the link's
fragment, before it shows the form, so it can say whose password it is
about to set. Nothing is consumed: the same token can be checked again
until it is used, replaced or expired.

A link is a one-time secret an Admin or the account's owner had emailed
(D15). It works once, for 24 hours, and a newer link for the same
account replaces it.

**Leak review (§6.5).** An unknown, used, expired or revoked token, and
the token of a disabled account, all answer the same `410
SET_PASSWORD_LINK_INVALID`, with the same message, from the same single
indexed lookup, so the answer says nothing about which of them it was.
The lookup is an equality on the SHA-256 of a 256-bit token, which is
all the database keeps, so its timing reveals nothing usable. A valid
token is answered with the account's own email and name: the caller
already holds the secret that controls that account. The token is never
logged, is never in a query string and never reaches a `Referer`, since
the page sends it in this body only.

200.description: The link can still be used.

410.description:
`SET_PASSWORD_LINK_INVALID` — the link is unknown, used, expired or
revoked, or its account is disabled. The client says the link has
expired or was already used and asks the user to request a new one.

413.description: The body is over 8 KiB, which the rate limiter's keys read in full.

post.summary: Set a password from an emailed link, and sign in
post.description:
Sets the account's password, clears `mustChangePassword`, signs the
account in and answers as `login` does. The link has just proved
control of the mailbox, so no other proof is asked for.

One statement claims the token, so two submits at once set the password
once and the second is answered `410`. Setting a password also ends the
account's other sessions and links: it revokes every refresh family,
moves `session_epoch`, and revokes the account's other unused links, all
before the new session is issued. A Google-only account that sets a
password this way keeps its Google link.

**Leak review (§6.5).** The same single `410` as `checkSetPasswordLink`
for every invalid state. `422 PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_DISABLED` is decided
before the token is looked up, so it is the same for every caller and
says nothing about any token or account. A token that is not valid is
refused before any password is hashed, so the endpoint is no way to
spend the server's hashing capacity. The token is never logged, is never
in a query string and never reaches a `Referer`.

newPassword.description:
The same rule as `changePassword`: at least 8 characters,
at least one of which is a digit, a punctuation mark or a
symbol, in any script.

200.description: The password is set and the account is signed in. Sets the rotating refresh cookie.

413.description: The body is over 8 KiB, which the rate limiter's keys read in full.

422.description:
`PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_DISABLED` — the centre has turned password
sign-in off, so there is no password to set. The client sends the
person to sign in with Google.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token
post.description:
Reads the opaque token from the cookie and rotates it. Presenting an
already-rotated token revokes the **whole family** and forces re-login
(§5.2).

The client must call this **single-flight** — one shared in-flight
promise. Parallel calls on a cold page load would each present the same
token, trip reuse detection, and log the user out on every load.

Set-Cookie.description:
The REPLACEMENT `quizzivy_refresh` cookie. Rotation is only
half-done without it: the predecessor is revoked server-side, so
a client that kept the old value is logged out on its next call.

401.description:
Absent, expired, revoked, or reused. Client clears state and goes to `/login`.

**Leak review.** `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` when §5.2 reuse detection
fires, `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` otherwise — including for a suspended
account, which is not disclosed here any more than it is at login.

Distinguishing reuse does tell whoever presented the token that the
replay was noticed. That is accepted: by then the family is revoked,
so the information arrives with no access attached. The reason to
separate them is the victim, not the attacker — "someone else used
your session" is a message a student can act on, and "your session
expired" is not. The revocation is also written to `audit_log`.

get.description: Called on app load. A 401 sends the client to `/login` (§5.4).

patch.description:
Updates only supplied profile fields. Omission preserves a field;
null clears displayName or phone. Names are trimmed, while phone
keeps the literal accepted pattern. timeZone must be a valid stable
IANA zone or UTC; blank and Local are refused. Email, role, password,
provider links and photo changes use their separate operations.

200.description: The whole persisted caller profile and permissions.

post.description:
Revokes the presented refresh token family. The client also clears its
store and calls `queryClient.clear()` (§5.4).

Authenticated by the refresh COOKIE, not the access token. An expired
access token must not be able to strand a live refresh family: the one
moment a user most wants to log out is the moment their session has
gone strange.

A logout that is refused or fails still clears the refresh and docs
cookies when the request carried the refresh cookie: during a
maintenance window (`503 MAINTENANCE`), over the rate limit
(`429 RATE_LIMITED`) and when the revoke fails (`500 INTERNAL`). In
none of the three is the family revoked: this device is signed out,
but a copy of the token held elsewhere stays usable for as long as it
is rotated, and only a password reset, a disable or a password change
ends it. A request without the cookie gets nothing cleared.
post.summary: Revoke the refresh family and clear the cookie

204.description:
Revoked, and the cookie is cleared. Returned even for a token that
was already expired or revoked — logging out is idempotent, and
reporting "that token was not valid" would answer a question the
caller has no business asking.

401.description: No refresh cookie was presented, so there is no session to end.

post.summary: Change own password
post.description:
Clears `mustChangePassword` and revokes every **other** refresh family
for this user, so a second device is signed out.

The calling session is identified by the refresh cookie, which reaches
this endpoint because it is scoped `Path=/auth`. Without it the server
cannot tell the caller's family from a stranger's and revokes them all,
signing the caller out too.

currentPassword.description:
Required, EXCEPT while `mustChangePassword` is true.

In that window the current password is one a teacher
generated and read aloud, so re-entering it proves nothing
the access token has not already proved — and demanding it
strands the case G-07 is drawn for: a student whose password
was reset, who then signs in with Google and is redirected
here without ever having held the temporary one.

newPassword.description:
At least 8 characters, at least one of which is a digit, a
punctuation mark or a symbol, in any script. It must also
differ from the password it replaces, which only the server
can check (`PASSWORD_UNCHANGED`). The rules apply to a new
password only: existing passwords are never re-checked and
sign-in does not change.

204.description: Changed. The calling session survives; every other one is revoked.

400.description:
`INVALID_CREDENTIALS` — `currentPassword` is wrong.
`PASSWORD_REQUIRED` — the account signs in with Google only and has
no current password to verify; it needs a set-password flow, not this one.
`PASSWORD_UNCHANGED` — `newPassword` is the password it would replace:
the verified `currentPassword`, or, while `mustChangePassword` is set,
the temporary password on the account.
`VALIDATION_FAILED` — `newPassword` breaks a rule above.

**A wrong current password is deliberately 400, not 401.** The SPA
treats 401 as "the session died": it refreshes once and retries, and
a second 401 signs the user out (§5.2, `client.ts`). Returning 401
here would mean mistyping your own password rotates your refresh
token and then logs you out — with no hint that the typo was the
cause. 401 on this endpoint means the SESSION is invalid, nothing else.

post.summary: Email the caller a link to set a password
post.description:
For an account that signs in with Google and has no password: emails
the account's own address a link, valid once for 24 hours, that opens
the set-password page. A newer link replaces an earlier unused one. The
caller stays signed in; using the link later ends the other sessions,
as setting a password does.

The answer is `204` once the message is queued; delivery is by the
outbox and may follow a moment later. Nothing in the answer says
whether the address received it.

422.description:
`PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_DISABLED` — the centre has turned password
sign-in off, so a password would be of no use.

501.description: This server has no key to seal a link with (`SECRETS_KEY`), so it cannot send one.

post.summary: Link Google to the current account
post.description:
Same `email_verified` rule as sign-in (§5.1), and the same sign-in
policy: with Google sign-in off, or an address outside the allowed
domains, nothing is linked (`403`).

200.description:
Linked, or already linked to this same Google account — re-linking
is a no-op success rather than a conflict.

401.description:
The session is invalid, or the exchange failed, or `email_verified`
was false — the same §5.1 rule sign-in applies, for the same reason:
an unverified address is not evidence of anything, and binding one
to an existing account is the takeover path with the account
already chosen.

409.description:
`IDENTITY_ALREADY_LINKED` covers three cases, all of which mean
"this link cannot be made":

- that Google account is already bound to another user;
- this account already has a *different* Google account linked
  (D-08 allows one, so that "unlink" is unambiguous);
- the Google address is already some other account's email.

The third is refused for where it leads rather than where it starts.
Linking binds the Google `sub` to this account, and §5.3's first
branch matches on `sub` before email — so the owner of that address
signing in with their own Google would land in someone else's
account. Silent, and very hard to diagnose from the inside.

403.description:
`GOOGLE_SIGN_IN_DISABLED` — the centre has turned Google sign-in
off. `GOOGLE_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` — the verified address is outside
the centre's allowed domains.

delete.description:
**Rejected if it would leave no login method** (§15). A Google-only
account cannot unlink, and neither can an account whose password
cannot be used because the centre has turned password sign-in off; the
client disables the control and explains why.

409.description: `LAST_LOGIN_METHOD` — the account has no password to fall back to, or the centre has turned password sign-in off.

get.description:
Every live session of the caller, one row per sign-in, and no one
else's. The session of the request's refresh cookie comes first with
`current: true`; the others follow by `lastUsedAt`, newest first, then
by `familyId`. At most 100 rows: a caller with more sees the newest
ones, and "sign out the others" still ends them all.

The calling session is identified by the refresh cookie, which reaches
this endpoint because it is scoped `Path=/auth`. Without a cookie that
names a live session of the caller, the list is still returned and no
row is current.

**Leak review.** Each row holds a handle, a label built from a closed
list of names, a city and a country code, and a time, all of the
caller's own session. A row holds no IP address, no raw user agent, no
token or hash and no expiry. The location is the approximate place of
the last sign-in or refresh, which the caller can already see on their
own device. Responses are `no-store`.

post.summary: Sign out every other device
post.description:
Revokes every live session of the caller except the calling one, and
only when there is one to revoke also moves the caller's session epoch
and forgets the cached principal, so the access tokens of the sessions
that ended stop working at once on the server that took the request
and within 10 seconds on any other (§5). The epoch is the caller's,
so the caller's own access token is refused on its next request as
well; the client's single-flight refresh replaces it and the calling
session keeps its place. With nothing to revoke nothing is written, the
epoch does not move and `revoked` is 0.

The calling session is identified by the refresh cookie. When the
request carries none that names a live session of the caller, the
answer is `401 UNAUTHORIZED` and nothing is written: the server cannot
tell the caller's session from the others, and a holder of an access
token alone is not enough to sign an account out everywhere.

Limited to 5 a minute and 30 an hour per signed-in user.

revoked.description: How many sessions this call ended.

delete.description:
Revokes one live session of the caller, moves the caller's session
epoch and forgets the cached principal in the same command, so the
access tokens of every session of the caller are refused on their next
request, at once on the server that took the request and within 10
seconds on any other (§5). The sessions that were not revoked refresh
and carry on; the revoked one cannot refresh.

The id of another user's session, of one that is revoked or expired and
of one that never existed answer alike: `404 NOT_FOUND`. The calling
session is refused with `409 SESSION_IS_CURRENT`; signing out of it is
`POST /auth/logout`.

The calling session is identified by the refresh cookie. When the
request carries none that names a live session of the caller, the
answer is `401 UNAUTHORIZED` and nothing is written.

Limited to 10 a minute and 60 an hour per signed-in user.

Every tag reachable through the CURRENT status and

delete.description: Permanently deletes an archived test and its unused versions. Assignments or attempts referencing the test block deletion.

409.description: The resource is still referenced or has not reached its required inactive state.

get.description: Full test including the draft outline. Published content lives in versions, not here.

patch.summary: Update metadata and the draft outline
patch.description:
Backs the builder's 1.5s-debounced autosave (§8). The whole outline —
sections and question ordering — is written in one transaction.

`expectedUpdatedAt` is a version guard. §1.3 rules out real-time
collaborative authoring; this makes a stale second tab fail loudly with
`STALE_WRITE` instead of silently reverting the outline.

outlineFormat.description: Complete mixed-unit outline. Every section must include units and every existing owned group exactly once. Group deletion uses its dedicated revision-checked endpoint.

questionIds.description: Standalone question projection, in the same order as question units when outlineFormat is group_v1.

units.description: Required in every section with group_v1. Moves complete groups only within this test; cross-test reuse requires an independent copy.

409.description: `STALE_WRITE` — edited elsewhere since `expectedUpdatedAt`; `GROUP_OUTLINE_REQUIRED` — a legacy question-only outline cannot replace a draft containing shared groups. Metadata-only updates remain supported. `TEST_ARCHIVED` — restore the test before a mixed-outline edit.

post.summary: Move a question across a shared-context group's boundary, or within it
post.description:
Backs the builder's drag of a question into a shared-context group,
out of one, between two groups of the same test, and within one group.
It acts on this test's draft only: the question is a standalone unit
of a section of this test or a member of a group a section of this
test owns, and the destination is a section or a group that section
owns. A bank group is neither. Moving a standalone question to a
standalone place is the outline writer's job (`updateTest`), not this
operation's.

- **Into a group** (a standalone question, `to.groupId` set): the
  group gets a **copy** of the question, with fresh question, option
  and blank ids; the section's reference to the bank question is
  removed and the bank question itself is not touched. The copy
  remembers that bank question, which is what lets it go back as the
  original when it is dragged out unedited. The result's `questionId`
  is the copy's id and `copied` is true.
- **Out of a group** (a member, `to.groupId` null): a member that was
  copied into the group from a bank question, has not been edited
  since, and whose original is still in the bank, in the caller's
  reach and not already in this test, goes back as that original: the
  copy is removed, the original becomes a standalone unit of
  `to.sectionId` at `to.index`, no bank question is added, and
  `restored` is true with `questionId` the original's id. Any other
  member keeps its id and becomes an ordinary question of the bank, a
  standalone unit of `to.sectionId` at `to.index`; `editedCopy` is true
  when it had been copied from a bank question that is still there and
  was edited since. `copied` is false either way. A member that a gap
  of the group's shared material is bound to cannot leave (`422`,
  `details.rule` `group_gap_bound`).
- **Between groups of this test, or within one group** (a member,
  `to.groupId` set): the member moves in place, keeping its id and
  the link to the bank question it was copied from, if any. `copied`,
  `restored` and `editedCopy` are false.

`to.index` is the position among the section's units when
`to.groupId` is null, and among the group's members otherwise, counted
once the question has left its old place. A position past the end is
clamped to the end.

The move is guarded exactly as `updateQuestionGroup` guards a save:
`expectedUpdatedAt` is the test revision, and
`expectedGroupRevisions` names the revision of every group the move
touches, the source and the destination, once each, and no other. A
touched group missing from the list is `STALE_WRITE`; a group the move
does not touch, or one named twice, is a `400`. The answer carries the new
test revision and every touched group at its new revision, so the
builder goes on from them. Nothing is written when the move is
refused. No published version is touched; the next publish freezes
the new structure.

200.description: Moved. The saved draft and every touched group, at their new revisions.

400.description:
The body fails its schema (`to.index` below zero, more than two
group revisions, an unknown field); or the move itself is not one
this operation makes. `details.rule` names the case:
`move_outline_only` — a move between two standalone places, which
`updateTest` writes; `move_group_section` — `to.groupId` is a
group that `to.sectionId` does not own; `move_revisions` —
`expectedGroupRevisions` names a group twice, or names a group the
move does not touch; `move_source_ambiguous` — the question is a
standalone unit of more than one section of the test, which the
request cannot tell apart.

404.description: The test, the question, the section or a group is outside the caller's reach, or is not of this test. Another teacher's id answers exactly as a missing one does. An entry of `expectedGroupRevisions` is a group like any other, so one the caller cannot reach answers 404 before any revision is compared.

409.description: `STALE_WRITE` — the test was edited elsewhere since `expectedUpdatedAt`, or a touched group is past its expected revision or missing from `expectedGroupRevisions`; `TEST_ARCHIVED` — restore the test before moving a question; `GROUP_CONFLICT` — a uniqueness constraint refused the write because another writer got there first, and nothing is written.

422.description:
Validation failed and nothing was written. `details.rule` names
the rule: `group_gap_bound` — the member a gap of the group's
shared material is bound to cannot leave its group, and
`details` also carries `stimulusId`, `gapId` and `questionId`;
or any rule the destination group fails once the question is in
it (`group_limits` at 200 members or the 4 MiB budget,
`group_audio_scope` when the copied question uses the group's own
shared recording, `group_asset`); or `group_reference` — a
database reference or check refused the write, as it does an
`updateQuestionGroup` that drops a member something still uses.

post.summary: Validate and snapshot a new version
post.description:
Validates, snapshots resolved content into the version tables, bumps
`currentVersion` and writes an audit row — all in one transaction.

Snapshotting is what makes editing a published test safe: in-flight and
historical attempts keep rendering the version they started with (§7).
`mediaAssetId` points at the same immutable asset; the file is never
copied (§11.1).

Republishing an unchanged test still creates a version — this is an
append-only history, not a diff.

The body is optional. `changeNote` is kept with the version and is
trimmed first; a note that is empty after trimming is no note.

changeNote.description: What changed in this version, in the teacher's words. Shown in the version history. The 200-character limit applies to the text as sent, before it is trimmed.

409.description:
`PUBLISH_VALIDATION_FAILED`. **Every** problem is returned at once,
each anchored to a question, so the builder marks them inline rather
than surfacing one per attempt (§8).

A question whose media file has been deleted from the library (rule
`audio_question_has_asset` for audio, `question_valid` for any other
file), or a group whose material names one (`group_valid`), is
reported the same way, but only once the draft passes every other
rule: the files are checked when the version is frozen.

post.description: Copies the draft structure only — never the versions. The copy starts as a draft.

get.description: Backs §8's test-detail version history. Spec §15 has no endpoint for this.

delete.description: Deletes an unused, non-current version. Existing assignments and attempts prevent deletion.

get.summary: What changed between a version and another paper
get.description:
Compares the version in the path with another paper of the same test
and lists what a teacher would call a change. The older paper is
`from` and the newer `to`; the draft is always the newer. Reads only:
nothing is written, and no row is locked.

Questions are matched by the bank question they were frozen from, and
the ones left over by identical content, because restoring a version as
a draft copies its questions. So a question that was restored and then
edited reads as `removed` and `added`, not as `changed`. Order alone is
never a change.

parameters.name: against
parameters.description:
`previous` is the highest version below the path version, so the
path version is `to`; on the first version there is none, `from` is
null and every question is `added`. `draft` is the test's draft, so
the path version is `from`. A number is another version of the test:
the lower of the two is `from`. The path version itself is refused
with 400, and a version that does not exist is 404.

422.description: A group of one of the two papers cannot be read, so there is no paper to compare. For the draft (`against=draft`) the builder reports the cause when the teacher publishes; for a version it is stored data that no longer reads back.

still used elsewhere (`RESOURCE_REFERENCED`): the draft is left as
it was.

Every tag reachable through the CURRENT type, audio and

collected from the returned page: a rail built from one
page can only offer the tags that page happens to carry,
which makes a second chip unselectable and the filter

The tag filter itself is not applied, for the same

on that line, "đang lọc 41": rows matching ALL current

forty questions at a time, and doing it one at a time is what the
selection bar exists to avoid.

Additive and idempotent: a tag a question already carries is a no-op, so
a retry after a dropped connection cannot duplicate anything. Removing

post.summary: Upload a private Word or PDF source and create an immutable source set
post.description:
One multipart file part named file, at most 25 MiB. The filename ends in
.docx or .pdf, or in .doc when legacy conversion is enabled (see limits), and
the detected content must agree with it. A PDF is read from its text layer;
a scanned PDF fails processing with PDF_NO_TEXT, unless the import was
created with readWithAi, in which case its pages are read by the AI
assistant (at most 40 pages, else PDF_TOO_LONG_FOR_AI).
The body Content-Type is not evidence of the detected document type.
Retry with identical uploadId, role, expectedRevision, filename and bytes.
A changed replay conflicts. Completion creates exactly one source revision;
replay returns its receipt even when later uploads advanced the import.
Uploads are accepted while the import awaits sources, has failed or is under
review; a new source set returns it to awaiting_sources, and processing again
keeps teacher edits. Every storage write first has a durable reservation;
interruptions remain inspectable and quota-counted.
Source bytes and storage keys never enter ordinary logs or student payloads.

The default raw JSON body limit applies independently of text length.
Identical normalized text with the same uploadId and expectedRevision replays
the original immutable receipt; changed content conflicts. Quotas, intake
capacity, ownership and retention are shared with file uploads.

post.description:
Creates the test, its sections, groups and bank questions in one
transaction; nothing persists on failure. Excluded questions are left out.
Replaying the same request after success returns the same test.

404.description: IMPORT_NOT_PROCESSED — no draft yet, or import not found.
