get.description:
The §8 media library: the caller's own files, whatever the caller
holds, newest first. A deleted file is not listed, and neither is one
that was replaced. Each row carries how many questions use it and how
many published versions reference it, so a file that cannot be deleted
can be shown as such. `q` is matched on `displayName` and on
`originalFilename`, without accents and without case.

parameters.name: unused
parameters.description:
`true` keeps only the files whose `questionCount` is zero. `false`
is the same as leaving it out. A file that only a published
version or an empty group still holds is unused here, and
`deleteMedia` still refuses it.

totalBytes.description:
Every file the search and the filters match, not
just this page, for A-07's "18 tệp · 42 MB". `total`
follows them in the same way.

Cache-Control.description:
`private, no-store`. Every item carries a signed URL with the
same ten-minute life as `/app/media/{assetId}/url`, so a cached
page would keep showing URLs that stopped working — and unlike
the single-URL response there is nothing worth re-serving, since
the library changes on every upload and delete. `no-store`
rather than `max-age` for that reason (§11.2).

post.summary: Upload an audio or image asset
post.description:
Upload goes **through the backend** in v1 — volume is low, and the
backend must validate anyway. Presigned direct-to-R2 is the P1
optimisation, and the client contract will not change beyond this one
call (§11.1).

The file part is streamed to disk and never held in memory.
Audio is mp3 or m4a, at most 50 MB and 5 minutes; an image is png,
jpg or webp, at most 10 MB (`MediaAsset`'s `x-media-limits`).
Validation order is the audio size → magic bytes → the image size →
duration, so an oversized upload is cut off before anything is parsed.
**Never trusts the `Content-Type` header or the file extension**
(§11.1): the type comes from sniffing, and the duration from probing
the container. An image's pixel size is read from its header; an image
whose header cannot be read is stored without one.

The file joins the caller's library, which may hold at most the
deployment's quota (`listMedia`'s `usage.quotaBytes`); a file that
would take it past the quota is not kept. The quota counts the files
in the library and the replaced or deleted files that something still
uses (`usage.heldBytes`).

Assets are immutable. Re-uploading the same file creates a new row with
a new key; it never overwrites (§11.1). That is what lets a version
snapshot reference an asset without copying the file.

parameters.name: defaultMaxPlays
parameters.description:
The default play limit to store with the audio, as
`LibraryAsset.defaultMaxPlays` reads it; `0` is unlimited. Left
out, none is set. Audio only: sent with a file that turns out to
be an image, the upload is refused and nothing is stored.

409.description:
`MEDIA_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — the caller's library, with the files it
still holds, would hold more than its quota with this file.
Nothing was stored.

413.description:
`MEDIA_TOO_LARGE` — over 50 MB, or an image over 10 MB (§11.1).
The message names the limit that was passed.

415.description:
`MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` (not mp3/m4a — §11.1 and §17.3),
`MEDIA_TOO_LONG` (over 5 minutes), or `MEDIA_UNREADABLE` (sniffed
correctly but the duration could not be probed — rejected rather
than stored with an unknown duration).

post.summary: Replace a library file without changing published versions
post.description:
Creates a new immutable file of the same kind, retaining the old owner's
display name and default play limit. Repoints that owner's editable
questions and bank or draft-owned groups atomically. Published versions,
other owners' rows and import review documents retain the old live file.
The old file leaves the library but remains readable and bindable.

What becomes of the old file is `previous`. While a published version or
another owner's content still uses it, it stays in storage and keeps
counting toward the owner's quota (`listMedia`'s `usage.heldBytes`).
Seven days after nothing uses it, it is removed from storage for good;
nothing restores it, and `previous.url` is the chance to download it.
Missing, foreign, deleted and already replaced IDs answer the same 404
before multipart bytes are read, after routing, authentication and header validation.
Audio is mp3 or m4a, at most 50 MB and 5 minutes; an image is png,
jpg or webp, at most 10 MB (MediaAsset's x-media-limits). Identification
and streamed validation match uploadMedia; kind is checked before storage.
Quota is the old owner's: the library with the new file in it, and the
old file only while something still uses it, so a replacement that
published versions hold needs room for both files. Every changed group
revision advances once, so cached question and group data must be reloaded.
A caller may replace ten files a minute and sixty an hour; beyond that
the answer is 429 with `Retry-After`, before the file is read.
This operation is not idempotent. An uncertain commit or a committed
replacement whose response fails returns an internal error and retains
the new object; retrying the old ID may answer 404. Failed storage
compensation also returns an internal error, without public internal details.

201.description: Replaced; asset is the new library file under the retained name.

409.description: MEDIA_QUOTA_EXCEEDED — the old owner's library would exceed its quota, counting the old file while something still uses it; no replacement committed and fresh-object compensation succeeded.

413.description:
`MEDIA_TOO_LARGE` — over 50 MB, or an image over 10 MB (§11.1).
The message names the limit that was passed.

415.description:
`MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` (not mp3/m4a — §11.1 and §17.3),
`MEDIA_TOO_LONG` (over 5 minutes), or `MEDIA_UNREADABLE` (sniffed
correctly but the duration could not be probed — rejected rather
than stored with an unknown duration). `MEDIA_KIND_MISMATCH` means
the identified file differs from the old asset's kind.

patch.summary: Rename a file or set its default play limit
patch.description:
Changes the name the library shows for a file and the default play
limit stored with it; the stored file and its `originalFilename` never
change, and neither does a question that uses it. It reaches the
caller's own file, or any file with `scope.all`, as `deleteMedia`
does. A missing, deleted or replaced file, and another owner's,
answer the same 404. The change is audited.

200.description: The file as the library now lists it.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes an unreferenced asset: it leaves the library at once and
its object is removed from storage seven days after nothing uses it,
which `deleteMedia` has just checked for published versions and
independent groups. Nothing restores it; the answer's `url` is the
chance to download it. A file a live question outside any group still
attaches keeps counting toward the quota (`listMedia`'s
`usage.heldBytes`) and is removed seven days after that stops.

200.description: Deleted; the answer says when the file's object goes.

409.description:
`MEDIA_REFERENCED` — a published version or independent question group still uses it (§8, §15).
`details.tests` names those versions as `ReferencingTest[]`,
sorted by title then version (A-07). `details.groups` names protected
draft/bank context as `ReferencingGroup[]`, sorted by title then ID.

get.description:
Backs the §8 assignments list. `status` is derived per assignment, not
stored (D-18). The list holds the assignments the caller created and
those that target a class the caller teaches, for every caller:
`scope.all` does not widen it. A row names only the target classes and
students the caller reaches, and `targetCount` counts those; for a
caller who holds `scope.all` that is every target, as in
`getAssignment`.
`classId` narrows the list to assignments that target
any of the classes named, one or several (G-06's "Xem tất cả", G-12);
the facets follow it, so the tab counts are those of the classes and
never disagree with the rows. A class named twice, in whatever spelling
of its id, answers 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. A class the caller does not
teach lists nothing, as a missing class does, unless the caller holds
`scope.all`: it then lists those of the caller's own assignments that
target it.
`q` keeps the assignments whose test title, or the name of a target
class the caller reaches, contains the text; it is accent-insensitive
and the facets follow it too. Every row carries `questionCount`.

post.description: Only a **published** version may be assigned (§8).

409.description: `TEST_NOT_PUBLISHED`.

get.summary: Download the results of up to 50 assignments as a CSV file
get.description:
One row per student of each assignment the caller reaches, in the order
of `ids` and then by name, for the students the caller reaches: the
roster the assignment's Students tab draws, so a student who has not
started has a row. The attempt that stands for a student is the one
that tab shows: their latest attempt that is not voided, else the
latest. Columns: Assignment (the test's title), Version, Class (the
target classes the caller reaches that the student belongs to, joined
by `; `), Student, Email, Status, Score, Max, Percent (score over max,
one decimal), Submitted (in the caller's own time zone, named in the
header; the default zone when the stored one is invalid), Focus lost
and Flagged. Score, Max and Percent are empty until every manually
marked answer of the attempt has a mark. Headers and the Status and
Flagged words follow `Accept-Language`, Vietnamese by default.

The file is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark and CRLF line ends, so
spreadsheets open it correctly. A cell that a spreadsheet would run as
a formula (it starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage
return, also after leading spaces, or with the full-width forms of the
first four) is written with a leading `'`. Overdue attempts are closed
before the file is read, as the monitor does.

An id the caller does not reach answers 404 for the whole request, as
a missing one does. More than 20000 rows answer 422. The response is
`private, no-store`, and a caller is limited to 10 files a minute and
60 an hour.

422.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED` — the assignments hold more than 20000 rows; `details.ids` says so. Pick fewer.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a draft or closed assignment with no attempts. Open or scheduled assignments and any historical attempts block deletion.

409.description: The resource is still referenced or has not reached its required inactive state.

get.description: A single assignment with its targets, window, and review and integrity policies.

patch.description:
`testVersionId` may be changed **only while no attempt exists**.
Re-pointing an untouched assignment at a corrected version is a
legitimate workflow; doing it once students have started is not.
Existing attempts always carry their own version regardless (§7).

While the assignment is `open`, a **change** to `testVersionId`,
`durationMinutes` or `maxAttempts` is refused with `ASSIGNMENT_LOCKED`
(DG-65: only "Test & timing" locks); sending the stored value passes,
and every other field stays editable. Outside `open` the version check
above is the only one.

A **closed** assignment, by its window or by an early close, at the
moment of the request, stays closed: a `window` that would make it
`scheduled` or `open` again, or that opens after the early close the
assignment keeps, is refused with `ASSIGNMENT_CLOSED`, because that is
a reopening and `reopenAssignment` does it, asking for a reason and
writing its own audit entry. A request that leaves it closed passes:
the stored window, an earlier `closesAt`, `closeNow` (while `opensAt`
is not ahead of now) and every other field. An early close is never
lifted here.

`review.release`, `review.showClassAverage` and `studentNote` are
partial: omitted, they keep what is stored. `studentNote: null` clears
the note. Every other field is replaced as before.

An attempt already in progress moves with a later close, in the same
transaction: its deadline becomes the earlier of its start plus the
student's time limit and the student's own close, when that is later
than the deadline it has. A deadline never moves earlier, so a shorter
close, or `closeNow`, leaves every attempt in progress where it is, and
an attempt whose deadline has already passed is over and is not
revived. Each attempt moved is audited as `attempt.extended`.

409.description:
`ASSIGNMENT_LOCKED` — the assignment is open, so the version, the
duration and the attempts cannot be changed; `ASSIGNMENT_CLOSED` —
the assignment is closed and the window would open it again, so it
is reopened with `reopenAssignment`; `VERSION_LOCKED` — attempts
exist, so the version cannot be changed; or `TEST_NOT_PUBLISHED`.

get.summary: Pending manual answers in grading order
get.description:
Read-only queue of reachable submitted or timed_out papers' saved answers
requiring manual grading with no manual score. Graded, voided, in-progress,
missing saved answers and marked zero scores are excluded. Normal
AssignmentIDs and Papers reach apply; scope.all widens the existing read.
Filters apply before complete counts, grouping and the first 200 items.
Groups order by their earliest known eligible submitted_at ascending,
all-null groups last, then student UUID or assignment/question UUID tuple.
Within a group items order by submitted_at ascending nulls last, attempt
UUID, paper ordinal and frozen question UUID. Only represented groups are
returned, with full remaining counts even when split at the cap.
Each supplied reference is independently checked: unknown and foreign
references answer the same 404, while reachable empty intersections are
empty successes. studentId selects an already authorized historical paper
taker, not a student-account target: it requires either a current strict
student-like account in StudentIDs reach or existing history satisfying
BOTH AssignmentIDs and Papers reach, independent of status or pending work.
A privileged account without reached history cannot use the strict branch.
Membership, counts, reference flags and prefix share one statement snapshot;
later immutable-content and signed-media enrichment is not a live whole
response snapshot. Names and titles are current text; question/group keys
and content are frozen. Grades and completion use existing gradeAttempt
and finishGrading; this read never writes or finishes a paper.

parameters.name: studentId
parameters.description: Historical paper-taker identity filter, not a strict student-account lookup.

200.description: Full filtered counts and the first 200 pending answers.

get.description:
G-04's "Chấm theo câu hỏi": one manually graded question across every
handed-in, non-voided attempt of the assignment, so the rubric is
decided once instead of per student. The write stays
`POST /teacher/attempts/{id}/grade`, one attempt per call. Rows come in
attempt order rather than by name, because the mode hides names until
the question is graded (anonymous marking).

manualQuestionIds.description: The paper's manually graded questions in paper order, for "Câu tiếp theo".

404.description: The assignment, or a question that is not on its paper.

post.summary: Copy an assignment as a draft
post.description:
Creates a **draft** that pins the same version and keeps the original's
time limit, attempts, shuffle flags, review options, integrity policy
and note to students, owned by the caller. Its window opens now and
lasts as long as the original's (`closesAt - opensAt`). It is assigned
to `classIds` and to no student by name; students never see a draft.
The original is not changed.

The original must be one the caller reaches, and its version one the
caller may assign (a published test of their own, or any under
`scope.all`): otherwise 409 `TEST_NOT_PUBLISHED`. A class the caller
does not teach answers 400 as an unknown one does.

409.description: `TEST_NOT_PUBLISHED` — the original's version is not one the caller can assign.

get.summary: How often students got each question wrong
get.description:
Every question of the pinned version, hardest first, over the papers
handed in by the students the caller reaches (see `handedIn`). Overdue
attempts are closed before it is read, as the monitor does. A question
no paper has a mark for sorts last with a null rate.

post.description:
G-09's "Gia hạn cho tất cả": a closed assignment gets a later
`closesAt` and its early close, if any, is lifted, so every student
with attempts left can go back in. Only a closed assignment can be
reopened, and only to a moment still ahead. Audited with the reason.

An attempt still in progress moves with it, in the same transaction,
as it does on `extendAssignment`: its deadline becomes the earlier of
its start plus the student's time limit and the student's own close,
when that is later than the deadline it has. An attempt whose deadline
has already passed is over and is not revived.

409.description: `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_CLOSED` — only a closed assignment has anything to reopen.

post.description:
Moves the assignment's `closesAt` later by `minutes`, for everyone. A
draft, a scheduled and an open assignment can be extended; a **closed**
one goes through `reopenAssignment` instead and answers
`ASSIGNMENT_CLOSED` here. Audited with the old and new close, in the
statement that moves it.

`notify` says the teacher wants the students told. It is recorded with
the audit entry. When it is true, each enabled student of a published
assignment whose own close the extension changed is sent an
`assignment.extended` notification naming the close they now have,
once the extension has committed: a student without an override, and
one whose override closes before the new close. A student whose
override closes at or after it keeps the close they had and is told
nothing. A failure to send is logged and never fails the extension.

An attempt already in progress moves with it, in the same transaction:
its deadline becomes the earlier of its start plus the student's time
limit and the student's own close, when that is later than the deadline
it has. A deadline never moves earlier, a student whose own
override already closes later keeps it, and an attempt whose deadline
has already passed is over and is not revived. Each attempt moved is
audited as `attempt.extended`. A student who starts afterwards gets the new
close, even if the start and the extension run at the same moment.

409.description: `ASSIGNMENT_CLOSED` — a closed assignment is reopened, not extended.

get.summary: The overrides on an assignment the caller reaches
get.description:
Every override on the assignment for a student the caller reaches, by
student name. It is not paged: an assignment holds at most one override
per targeted student.

put.description:
Gives each named student an override, or changes the one they have: a
later close, a longer time limit, more attempts, with the reason. It is
an accommodation, so it can open an assignment that has closed for
everyone else, for those students alone.

A field the request names replaces the stored one and a field it
leaves out keeps it, so lengthening a student's time does not take
away the attempts they were given. The reason always replaces; the
audit log keeps every earlier one. An override is removed with
`deleteStudentOverride`, not by sending zeros: a request that would
leave a row changing nothing is a `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

`closesAt` must be ahead of the database's clock. `extendBy` adds minutes to the student's
current close (their override's, when it is later, else the
assignment's) and is refused with `ASSIGNMENT_CLOSED` for a student
whose close has passed: a closed assignment is reopened for a student
with `closesAt`. A request names `extendBy` or `closesAt`, not both,
and at least one of the four. An override never shortens a close: the
later of it and the assignment's own is the student's.

Every id in `studentIds` must be a student of the assignment the caller
reaches: in a target class they teach or named on an assignment they
created, enabled, with a student role. One that is not answers `422
VALIDATION_FAILED` for the whole request and names the ids in
`details.studentIds`; nothing is written. A student who does not exist
and one the caller may not know exist answer the same.

Audited per student with the old and new values, in the statement that
writes them. `notify` is recorded with them. When it is true and the
request moves a close (`extendBy` or `closesAt`), each student named
whose override now closes after the assignment's own close is sent an
`assignment.extended` notification naming their close, once the
override has committed; more attempts or a longer time limit move no
close and tell nobody. A failure to send is logged and never fails the
request.

Each named student's attempt in progress moves with the override, as it
does on `extendAssignment`: its deadline becomes the earlier of its
start plus the student's time limit and the student's own close, when
that is later than the deadline it has. An attempt whose deadline has
already passed is over and is not revived.

200.description: The overrides as they now stand, by student name.

409.description: `ASSIGNMENT_CLOSED` — `extendBy` names a student whose close has passed.

422.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `details.studentIds` names the ids that are not students of this assignment the caller reaches.

delete.description:
Takes the override off one student: they have the assignment's own
window from then on. An override that does not exist is a 404, as one
on an assignment or a student the caller does not reach is. Audited
with the values removed. An attempt in progress keeps its deadline: a
deadline never moves earlier.

get.summary: Monitor rows, one per targeted student
get.description:
Includes students who have not started — the roster is the left side of
the join, not the attempts table. Two queries total, never one per
student: N+1 is the named default failure mode of this screen (§13.8).

The client polls every 15s while the assignment is `open`, and stops when
the tab is hidden (§8).

questionCount.description: Questions on the pinned version, the denominator of every row's progress.

get.description:
Backs §8's dashboard rows — attempts awaiting grading, flagged attempts —
which spec §15 has no endpoint for. `status=submitted` and `flagged=true`
each hit a partial index that stays near-empty (D-19).

get.summary: Full attempt for review and grading
get.description:
The teacher's view, so it carries the grading key: `AdminQuestion` includes
`isCorrect`, `sampleAnswer` and `acceptedAnswers`. This is the only
question shape that does.

audioPlays.description: Shown as used-vs-allowed, including over-limit. Reported, not enforced (§11.4).

teacherNote.description:
G-05's "Ghi chú của bạn": the teacher's private note on
this attempt. Teacher-only by construction — it lives on
this response and nowhere under `/app/*`.

get.description:
Integrity timeline, with paired durations computed server-side so the client
does not reimplement pairing (§10.4).

Events are grouped by session, ordered by each session’s earliest
received event time, with session ID breaking ties. Within a session,
resume events come first and session_takeover events last. Within that
priority, two events with different, non-null clientSeq values are
compared by clientSeq; otherwise they are compared by occurredAt, then
event ID. Current clients derive clientSeq from an attempt-relative
millisecond offset calibrated from serverTime, never below the tab’s
stored next sequence. This generally aligns separate tabs with elapsed
attempt time, but response latency, clock changes and per-tab increments
can cause reordering or collisions; chronology and uniqueness across
tabs are not guaranteed. Older counters can overlap newer values and
generally sort before offset-based events.

**The UI presenting this must be neutral** — no red banners, no
"CHEATING DETECTED". These signals are evidence for a conversation, not
proof: they cannot see a second device, a phone beside the laptop, a
person in the room, or a printed sheet (§10.5).

post.description:
May push the deadline past the assignment's `closesAt` — that is the
point of an accommodation. Audited in the same statement as the update,
via an `OLD`/`NEW` data-modifying CTE (§13.4).

409.description: `ATTEMPT_CLOSED` — only an attempt still in progress has a deadline to move.

post.description:
**Voids** the existing attempt and permits a new one at `attemptNo + 1`.
Nothing is deleted — §6.4's retention principle, and deleting would lose
the record §13.4 exists to keep (O-08).

409.description: `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` — already voided; nothing to reset.

post.description: Marks an attempt void with a required reason. Nothing is deleted, and the audit row is written in the same statement (§13.4).

409.description: `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` — already voided.

patch.description:
G-05's "Ghi chú của bạn": a note only the teacher reads, kept on the
attempt so it is there next term. `null` clears it. Never surfaces on
any `/app/*` response.

post.description:
G-05's "Đánh dấu" and "Bỏ đánh dấu": marks an attempt to look at
again, or clears the mark, by hand. A mark, not a verdict (§10.4).
Audited in the same statement as the update, as `attempt.flagged` or
`attempt.unflagged`, with the reason when one is given.

409.description: `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` — a voided attempt is out of the queue already.

post.summary: Save manual grades
post.description:
Saved per call rather than as one giant submit, so a half-graded attempt
survives a refresh. `points` is rejected above the question's ceiling.

409.description: `ATTEMPT_IN_PROGRESS` or `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` — nothing to grade yet, or nothing that counts.

post.description:
Recomputes the score from `SUM(final_score)` — the PG18 virtual generated
column, so manual precedence over auto cannot drift (§13.3) — and sets
status `graded`. Re-enterable: a graded attempt can be re-graded.

409.description: `GRADING_INCOMPLETE` — a `short_answer` is still ungraded; `ATTEMPT_IN_PROGRESS` / `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` as for grade.

get.description: The dashboard in the caller's own teaching scope, Admin included; the repository wide scope is never requested here.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Calendar range for submissions only; all other dashboard figures keep their own windows.

get.description:
Three nav counts in the caller's own teaching scope, Admin included; answersToGrade is null without teaching.grading.

`audience` narrows `unreadNotifications` to one console's kinds and
changes neither of the other two counts. The teacher's bell passes
`teacher`; without it the count is every kind the caller has.
Backs the §8 students table. CSV import is P1 and deliberately not built (§16).

parameters.name: classId
mustChangePassword
parameters.description:
`true` lists only the accounts still on a temporary password; after a
`resetStudentsPasswords` whose answer was lost, those are the students
whose password must be reset again. `false` lists only the others.
Absent lists both.

parameters.name: neverSignedIn
parameters.description:
`true` lists only the accounts that have never signed in
(`last_sign_in_at` is null); `false` lists only the others. Absent
lists both. It narrows beside `mustChangePassword`, as a plain
predicate: an account on a temporary password that never signed in
is in both.

parameters.name: accountStatus
parameters.description:
Only the accounts listed under one of these statuses
(`accountStatus=active&accountStatus=never_signed_in`), in
`AccountStatus`'s order of precedence. A `disabled` account is
returned only when `status` is `disabled` or `all`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Defaults to `active`. Without `disabled` there is no request that can
return a suspended account, so `updateStudent`'s `disabled: false`
would be unreachable.

post.description:
Teacher-created accounts get a temporary password and
`mustChangePassword` as the organization's "force password change"
setting says (on by default). Self-signup requires Google (§6.3).

Every `classIds` entry must be a class the caller teaches, or any class
with `scope.all`. Anything else answers 404, exactly as a missing class
does, and nothing is created.

201.description: Created. The temporary password is returned **once**.

409.description: `EMAIL_TAKEN` — already in use, compared case-insensitively.

post.summary: Reset the passwords of up to 40 students at once
post.description:
Does for each student what `resetStudentPassword` does, one transaction
each: a new temporary password, `mustChangePassword` set, every refresh
family revoked, the session epoch moved, one audit row. The same guards
apply to each student, in the same order (`student` in the caller's reach
and student-like, the subset rule, then the shared-student rule), so a
batch cannot do what one reset cannot.

A student that fails does not stop the others: `failed` names it with
`NOT_FOUND` (another teacher's student, a disabled one, a missing id, an
account that is not a student, all alike), `FORBIDDEN` (the student's
permissions are not a subset of the caller's), `STUDENT_SHARED` (someone
else also reaches the student, so only a holder of `people.users.manage`
may reset them) or `INTERNAL` (a fault with that student alone, logged on
the server). The answer is 200 whenever the request was accepted, even
when every student failed. `items` and `failed` keep the order of
`studentIds`.

Each `temporaryPassword` is returned **once** and stored nowhere: the
server keeps only its hash. A reset that committed before the connection
dropped has lost its password for good; those students are on a
temporary password, so `listStudents` with `mustChangePassword=true`
lists them for another reset. The answer is never cached. Repeating a
request resets the same students again with new passwords.

Limited to 2 a minute and 10 an hour per signed-in user, a call counting
once however many students it names.

200.description: The batch ran. Passwords are returned **once**.

get.description: A student with their class memberships, linked providers and `joinedVia` (§8).

patch.description:
Edits profile fields, or disables the account. Disabling blocks login
without deleting any attempt history. `disabled`, either value, also
needs `people.users.manage`. A new `email` needs `people.users.manage`
too unless no one else reaches the student, by the rule
`resetStudentPassword` states, because a new address can take over the
account through Google sign-in. Sending the address the student already
has is not a change. The student's permissions, except
`learning.take_tests`, must be a subset of the caller's.

403.description:
`FORBIDDEN` — `disabled` without `people.users.manage`, or a student
whose permissions are not a subset of the caller's.
`STUDENT_SHARED` — a new `email` for a student someone else also
reaches, without `people.users.manage`. Nothing is written.

409.description: `EMAIL_TAKEN` — another account already uses that address.

post.description:
Sets a temporary password and `mustChangePassword`. There is no
self-service email reset in v1 — that needs an email provider, which is
the same dependency §6.3 declines (§5.4, §17.1). Only a student no one
else reaches may be reset by a teacher: every class they are in,
archived ones included, is the caller's; no other account created them;
no other account's assignment targets them individually; and a student
in no class must have been created by the caller. A holder of
`people.users.manage` resets any student.

403.description:
`STUDENT_SHARED` — someone else also reaches the student, so only a
holder of `people.users.manage` may reset them. `FORBIDDEN` — the
student's permissions are not a subset of the caller's. Nothing is
written.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a disabled student account only when no assignment, attempt, retained audit record or owned content references it, and only when the student's permissions, except `learning.take_tests`, are a subset of the caller's. Historical identities use the approved manual anonymization process instead.

403.description: `FORBIDDEN` — the student's permissions are not a subset of the caller's.

409.description:
`RESOURCE_NOT_ARCHIVED` — the account is not disabled.
`RESOURCE_REFERENCED` — something still references it, and
`details.referencedBy` (`ReferencedBy`) always names what:
`assignments` (an individual assignment target, or an assignment it
created), `attempts`, `audit` (audit history it acted in),
`owned_content` (tests, questions, question groups, media, classes,
join codes, published versions or Word imports it owns or created),
or `other`.

get.summary: The roles and the permission catalogue
get.description:
Every role with its permissions, head count and revision, and the
catalogue of matrix rows, for the Roles & permissions page. The
Assistant is listed as the deck draws it; only the role pickers
(`listAssignableRoles`) leave it out.

post.summary: Create a custom role
post.description:
The new role takes the icon `key-round` and the colour `gray`, and starts
with the permissions of `copyFromRoleId`, if given. The source must pass
the subset rule: its permissions, `learning.take_tests` apart, are the
caller's own. The Assistant cannot be a source. A name and a description
are stored in Unicode NFC, so the composed and decomposed forms of one
name are the same name. The limits of 60 and 300 characters count the
text after NFC; the schema bounds the text as sent at four times that,
so a name typed decomposed is not refused before it is composed. A name
holds a letter, a digit, a punctuation mark or a symbol. Neither field
holds a control or invisible character: a zero-width one, a blank
filler such as the Hangul filler or the Braille blank, a lone code
point nothing assigns; a description may hold line breaks, a name may
not. At most 200 roles exist, the four built-in ones included; past that
the answer is `ROLE_LIMIT_REACHED`. Writes one audit row,
`role.created`.

403.description: `TARGET_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED` — the source role holds a permission the caller lacks.

409.description: `ROLE_NAME_TAKEN` — another role has the name, in any letter case.

422.description: `ROLE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE` — the source is the Assistant. `ROLE_LIMIT_REACHED` — 200 roles exist already.

get.summary: The roles the caller may give to a user
get.description:
The roles whose permissions, `learning.take_tests` apart, are a subset of
the caller's, without the Assistant, which no picker offers. For the Add
user dialog and the user sheet.

put.description:
Grants and revokes permissions across roles in one transaction, and
refuses the whole save when any change breaks a rule:

- `KEY_NOT_GRANTABLE` — a hidden key.
- `ROLE_LOCKED` — an Admin cell other than `learning.take_tests`.
- `STUDENT_NEEDS_TAKE_TESTS` — `learning.take_tests` off the built-in Student.
- `CANNOT_ACT_ON_SELF` — a change to the caller's own role, except the
  Admin role's `learning.take_tests` cell, which gives no power over anyone.
- `TARGET_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED` (403) — a role, or a key granted or revoked,
  that the subset rule keeps from the caller.
- `STALE_WRITE` (409) — a role is past its expected revision, or the
  save names no revision for it.

A change that leaves a cell as it was is accepted and writes nothing.
Everyone's permissions are read again on their next request on the
machine that served the save, and within about ten seconds on any other. Writes
one `role.permissions_changed` audit row per role changed.

403.description: `TARGET_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED` — the subset rule keeps the caller from a role or a key.

409.description: `STALE_WRITE` — a role changed since the matrix was read.

422.description: `KEY_NOT_GRANTABLE`, `ROLE_LOCKED`, `STUDENT_NEEDS_TAKE_TESTS` or `CANNOT_ACT_ON_SELF`.

patch.summary: Edit a role's name, description, icon or colour
patch.description:
A supplied field is changed and the others are kept; a body with only
`expectedRevision` is refused. A built-in role may be renamed; its key never changes. The target must pass the subset rule.
A name and a description are stored in Unicode NFC and follow the rules
of a role's creation: the limits count the text after NFC, a name holds
a letter, a digit, a punctuation mark or a symbol, and neither holds a
control or invisible character.
A change moves the revision. Writes one audit row, `role.updated`, naming
what changed.

403.description: `TARGET_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED` — the role holds a permission the caller lacks.

409.description: `STALE_WRITE` — the role changed since `expectedRevision`. `ROLE_NAME_TAKEN` — another role has the name, in any letter case.

get.description:
Everything the Overview draws in one read: the centre's name, how many
people and classes it holds, who was active on each of the last
fourteen days, what needs attention, the five newest audit entries and
the storage meters.

Each section is `null` for a caller who lacks its key, never an error,
so a custom role sees only what it may: `people` and `dailyActive` need
`people.users.manage`, `classes` needs `scope.all`, `recentChanges`
`system.audit.read` and `storage` `system.settings.write`. An attention
row is held to the key of the page it leads to: `must_change_password`
and `never_signed_in` need `people.users.manage`,
`disabled_teacher_classes` `scope.all`, `storage` `system.settings.write`
and `ai_credit_requests` `ai.credits.manage`, which exists only while the
AI assistant is configured. A row whose count is zero is left out.

Days are the local dates of the centre's `APP_TIMEZONE`, the same days
the activity table records. `people.activeThisWeek` counts the
distinct accounts active on any of the last seven of them, today
included.

The one count the Admin sidebar draws as a badge: the accounts that
must change their password (DG-54). It is the number the Overview's
`must_change_password` attention row carries, counted by the same rule.
`mustChangePassword` is `null` without `people.users.manage`, when the
count is not run.

get.summary: What the centre uses against its plan
get.description:
The Plan & usage figures. The plan and its limits come from the
server's `PLAN_*` configuration, each optional, and nothing here is
enforced (DG-55): a limit is shown, never applied. `aiCredits` is the
month's credits used against the centre pool, and is `null` without
`ai.credits.manage` and while the AI assistant is off.

post.summary: Open the API reference for fifteen minutes
post.description:
Sets `quizzivy_docs`, a docs-only session cookie. `/docs` and
`/docs/openapi.json` answer only to it: 401 without a valid one, 403 for
a role without `system.api_reference`. The cookie carries a token for the `docs`
audience signed with its own key, so it is never an access token and an
access token never opens the docs. `Path=/docs` keeps it off every API
request, and `SameSite=Strict` still travels on the SPA's same-site
navigation to the API origin. Admin only, through `system.api_reference`, and
rate-limited as an operation that mints a credential.

204.description: The docs session is open for fifteen minutes.

get.description:
The contract's OpenAPI and document versions, how many operations it
declares and, for each tag in the order the contract lists them, how
many operations carry it (an operation with two tags is counted under
both). It is read once from the spec the server embeds, so it always
describes the build that answers. The page draws its own names and
blurbs for the groups; this is the part only the server knows.

This file, `api/openapi.yaml`, converted to JSON with its keys, values
and order unchanged (DG-10), an attachment named `quizzivy-openapi.json`.
It is not the spec the server routes by, whose operation ids the code
generator has rewritten and whose descriptions beside a `$ref` it has
dropped. The body is that JSON document, declared as a byte stream so
the generated server writes it as it is and does not encode it a second
time. The response is
`no-store`. It needs the bearer token and `system.api_reference`,
unlike `/docs/openapi.json`, which answers to a docs session.

One page of the audit log, newest first, and how many entries each
category holds. The log is append-only: nothing here changes it.

**Range.** `range` is `today` (from midnight), `7d` (the last seven
calendar days, today included), `30d` (the last thirty), `all`, or
`custom`, which takes `from` and `to` as dates, both inclusive. Every
day is the viewer's own: their stored time zone, else the centre's
default. `from` and `to` without `custom`, `custom` without both, and a
`to` before `from` answer `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the field.

**Search.** `q` matches, without regard to case or accents, the actor's
name or email, the sentence that words the action in either language,
and the label of the user, class, test, assignment, attempt, media file,
import or question group an entry is about.

**Categories.** An entry's category follows from the kind of thing it
is about. Entries about the organization, exports, maintenance,
retention and the AI credits belong to no category: `category` is
`null` and only the unfiltered list holds them.

**Facets.** `facets` counts the entries that match the current `q` and
range and ignores `category`, so selecting one never zeroes the others;
`all` counts every such entry, those in no category included, so it can
exceed the sum of the six. `total` is the selected category's count, or
`all`.

**Entries.** `changes` lists the fields an entry changed, each with the
value it had and the value it has. `details` holds anything else the
entry recorded. A join code is shown as `••••-` and its last four
characters, and a password, token or secret is never shown. `label` is
`null` when the row the entry is about no longer exists.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of a `custom` range, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of a `custom` range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive.

get.description:
The entries of a period, newest first, as one file. `period` is the
last seven or thirty calendar days or the calendar year so far, counted
in the viewer's own time zone; `range`, `from` and `to` are not
parameters here. `category` and `q` narrow it as they narrow the list.

The file is an attachment named `audit-log-YYYYMMDD` with `.csv` or
`.json`, and the response is `no-store`. A CSV is UTF-8 with a
byte-order mark and CRLF line ends, headers in the viewer's language
by `Accept-Language`, and every cell that a spreadsheet would run as a
formula is written with a leading `'`. A JSON file is an array of the
entries `listAuditLog` returns. Both are streamed.

More than 100,000 entries answer `422 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE`, and the caller
is asked for a shorter period. Each file is itself audited as
`audit.exported`, with the period, the format and the number of rows.
A caller is limited to 5 files a minute and 30 an hour.

422.description: `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` — the period holds more than 100,000 entries.

post.summary: Ask for a full export of the centre's data
post.description:
Queues one export for the worker and answers at once. It builds a ZIP
of `users.csv` (no password hashes or tokens), `roles.csv`,
`classes.csv` (no join codes), `class_members.csv`, `tests.csv`,
`test_versions.csv`, `assignments.csv`, `attempts.csv`, with
`answers.csv` when `includeAnswers` is true, and a `README.txt` in
Vietnamese and English that describes each file. Every CSV is UTF-8
with a byte-order mark and CRLF line ends, and a cell that a
spreadsheet would run as a formula is written with a leading `'`.

Only one export runs at a time for the whole centre: while any is
queued or running, another request answers `409 EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS`.
When the file is ready the requester gets an email that links to the
app page `/admin/exports/{id}`, never to the file. The file can be
fetched up to three times, by the requester, within 24 hours
(`downloadDataExport`).
The request is audited as `data_export.requested`. A caller who has an
export from the last hour that has not failed (queued, running, ready
or fetched) is refused with `429 RATE_LIMITED` and `Retry-After`, the
seconds until that export is an hour old. A failed export, a request
refused with `409` and a request refused with `429` do not count.
Without object storage and the worker the answer is `501 EXPORT_OFF`.

409.description: `EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS` — an export is already queued or running.

get.description:
The state of an export the caller requested; another user's export
answers `404` exactly as a missing one does. A `ready` export whose
24 hours have passed reads `expired`, whether or not the housekeeping
has removed its file yet.

post.summary: Fetch an export, up to three times
post.description:
Hands the requester a presigned URL for the ZIP, valid for 60 seconds,
that forces an attachment named `quizzivy-export-YYYYMMDD.zip`. One
statement checks that the export is `ready`, unexpired and signed fewer
than three times, and counts the signing in `downloads`, so a failed
transfer can be tried again; the fourth request, and a request after the
24 hours, answer `410 EXPORT_UNAVAILABLE`. Another user's export answers
`404`. The response is `no-store`, because the URL is a credential. Each
signing is audited as `data_export.downloaded`, and a caller may fetch
ten an hour.

410.description: `EXPORT_UNAVAILABLE` — the export is not ready, has expired, failed, or was already signed three times.

get.description:
The pool, the teachers with their month, the requests waiting and the
rules in force. The projection is `used` over the days elapsed times
the days in the month, computed from the server's clock.

patch.description:
A supplied field is changed and the others are kept. A new default
allowance rewrites this month's allowances that are not custom, never
below what a teacher has already used. One audit row names the caller.

post.summary: Add credits to this month's pool
post.description:
How an Admin approves use beyond the plan: the pool is never overspent
without it. The credits do not carry into next month. The audit row
names the caller as the approver.

put.summary: Change a teacher's AI allowance, or pause or resume them
put.description:
Takes effect at once and usage so far still counts, so an allowance
below it is refused (`AI_ALLOWANCE_BELOW_USE`). Approved requests'
credits stay on top. Subject to the subset rule: the teacher's
permissions, except `learning.take_tests`, must be a subset of the
caller's (`FORBIDDEN`), as for a student's account. One audit row names
the caller.

200.description: The teacher's month after the change.

403.description: `FORBIDDEN` — the teacher's permissions are not a subset of the caller's.

404.description: No such teacher: the id names no active user who is not a student.

409.description: `AI_ALLOWANCE_BELOW_USE` — the allowance is below what the teacher has used or holds this month.

post.summary: Approve a request for more credits
post.description:
Raises the teacher's allowance for the request's month by the amount and
tells the teacher. Subject to the subset rule, as `setAiAllowance` is.
One audit row names the caller.

200.description: The decided request and the teacher's allowance.

403.description: `FORBIDDEN` — the teacher's permissions are not a subset of the caller's.

409.description:
`AI_REQUEST_DECIDED` — decided already. `AI_REQUEST_EXPIRED` — the
request is from an earlier month, whose allowance is no longer the
teacher's.

post.summary: Decline a request for more credits
post.description:
Changes only the request's status and tells the teacher. Subject to the
subset rule, as `setAiAllowance` is. One audit row names the caller.

403.description: `FORBIDDEN` — the teacher's permissions are not a subset of the caller's.

409.description: `AI_REQUEST_DECIDED` — decided already.

get.description: The whole settings document as stored, read from the database.

put.description:
Replaces the whole document when `expectedRevision` is the stored one,
and answers it as stored, its revision one higher. A logo is named by
the hash `uploadOrganizationLogo` answered; until a save names it, an
upload changes nothing. A policy that would leave the caller, or every
active built-in Admin, without a way to sign in is refused, judged
inside the save as `getSignInImpact` judges it. One audit row,
`organization.updated`, names the caller and the fields that changed.
Other servers apply the new document within 30 seconds.

200.description:
The document as stored. A document equal to the stored one changes
nothing: the same revision comes back and no audit row is written.

400.description:
The body fails its schema, or `VALIDATION_FAILED` with a message per
field: a text that is empty or too long after trimming, a name that
holds a line break or an invisible character, a website that is not a
domain or an `https` address without credentials, an email or a
phone number that is not one, a repeated domain, or a logo the server
does not hold (as `organization.logo.light` or `organization.logo.dark`).

409.description: `STALE_WRITE` — saved elsewhere since `expectedRevision`; read again.

422.description:
`SIGN_IN_POLICY_LOCKOUT` — the policy would leave the caller, or every
active built-in Admin, with no way to sign in. `details.affectedUsers`
and `details.affectedAdmins` count the active accounts it leaves
without one. Nothing was stored.

post.summary: What a sign-in policy would do to the active accounts
post.description:
Counts, without storing anything, the active accounts the proposed
policy would leave with no way to sign in, the built-in Admins among
them, and whether the caller is one. The settings page asks before it
offers Save; the save judges again.

post.summary: Upload a logo
post.description:
Stores a logo and answers its hash, which a save of the settings then
names; the upload alone changes nothing ("Logo uploaded. Save settings
to apply."). The object is content-addressed, so the same file uploaded
twice is stored once.

A PNG is at most 1 MiB, square within 2% and 256 to 2048 pixels a side.
Its type is read from its first bytes, its header before any pixel is
decoded, and it is decoded and encoded afresh, which drops every
metadata chunk. Any other type, an SVG included, answers
`MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED`: the settings page draws an SVG to a PNG in the
browser before it uploads (D-019). A caller
may upload 20 logos an hour.

The request may carry 16 KiB more than the 1 MiB file for the multipart
framing.

415.description:
`MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` (not a PNG), `MEDIA_UNREADABLE` (the header or
the pixels cannot be read) or `IMAGE_DIMENSIONS` (not square within 2%,
a side outside 256 to 2048 pixels, or needing more memory to decode
than the server allows). Nothing was stored.

501.description: Object storage is not configured, so no logo can be kept.

get.description:
Classes, newest first. Paginated and searchable like every other list:
§1.3 promised single-digit classes, and a development database already
holds over a hundred, which is what broke the class pickers.

**Codes.** Each item's `joinCode.code` is a bearer secret, so it is opened
only when the request says `withCodes=true`, which the class cards send and
the pickers do not. It is then the code exactly when `getJoinCode` would
read it for the same caller and class: the caller holds
`teaching.classes.write`, reaches the class, and the code is readable (not
a legacy code, and sealed under a key this server holds). In every other
case `code` is `null`, a missing permission included, which is not an
error. The answer is never cached, whether or not codes are asked for, and
the operation is limited like the others that reveal one: 60 a minute and
600 an hour per user.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Defaults to `active`, so every picker drops archived classes without asking (G-08).

parameters.name: withCodes
parameters.description: Open each item's join code. Only the screen that shows codes asks.

post.description: Creates a class. A join code is not issued automatically; rotate to get one (§6.4).

scheduleLabel.description: Plain text, trimmed by the server; omitted, `null` and blank are all none. The 120 characters are counted before trimming.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an archived class and its owned memberships/join codes. Assignment references block deletion; student accounts and papers are retained.

409.description:
`RESOURCE_NOT_ARCHIVED` — the class is not archived.
`RESOURCE_REFERENCED` — something still references it, and
`details.referencedBy` (`ReferencedBy`) always names what:
`assignments` (an assignment targets the class), `members` (a
membership in another class came through one of its join codes),
or `other`.

get.description: A single class, including its active join code metadata -- but never the code itself (§13.3).

patch.description: Edits name, description, schedule and room, toggles self-join, or archives and restores. Disabling self-join does not revoke the existing code; use the delete endpoint for that.

scheduleLabel.description:
Plain text, trimmed by the server; a value that is blank once
trimmed is the same as none. Omitted, the stored value is kept;
`null` or blank clears it. The 120 characters are counted before
trimming.

archived.description: true archives, false restores; either is idempotent.

get.description:
Shows `joinedVia` and `joinedAt` so the teacher can spot unexpected
enrolments — the mitigation §6.5 relies on instead of an approval queue.
Spec §15 has no endpoint for this. `q` searches name and email.

post.description:
Enrols an existing user directly, bypassing the join code. Recorded as
`joinedVia: admin` so the teacher can tell the two apart.

`userId` must be an active student the caller reaches. Anything else
answers 404, whatever the reason, so the answer reveals nothing about
accounts beyond the caller's reach.

delete.description:
Revokes access. **Attempts are retained, not deleted** (§6.4), and an
in-flight attempt is not revoked — eligibility is evaluated at attempt
creation.

Idempotent for a user who is not a member: the class ends up in the
requested state either way. A class that does not exist is still a 404,
so a typo in the URL does not look like it worked.

get.summary: Read the class's active join code
get.description:
The active code of a class the caller teaches, or of any class under
`scope.all`, with its metadata (D5). The code is a bearer secret: the
response is never cached, and the operation is rate-limited like every
other that reveals one. It is not audited, because the teacher's
screens show the code on every class card.

`code` is `null` when the code cannot be read back. A code issued
before v0.8.0 is held only as a hash (`legacy: true`), and R4 rotates
those. A code sealed under a key this server no longer holds
(`legacy: false`) can be neither read nor redeemed. Rotate either to
get a readable code.

404 when the class is not the caller's, exactly as a missing class
answers, or when it has no active code.

post.summary: Issue a new join code, revoking the old one
post.description:
Revoke-and-issue happens in **one transaction**, so the one-active-code-
per-class constraint cannot be violated. Previously enrolled students are
unaffected (§6.1).

An archived class is refused with `409 CLASS_ARCHIVED` and nothing is
written: its current code, if any, stays as it was. Nobody can join an
archived class, so a code issued for one would be a dead secret that
reads as live. The archived check runs after the class has been found
for the caller, so another teacher's archived class answers 404 exactly
as a missing one does. Restore the class (`updateClass` with
`archived: false`) to rotate again. `revokeJoinCode` stays allowed on an
archived class.

The plaintext code is returned here, and `getJoinCode` reads it again.
It is stored encrypted under a key the database does not hold, with a
keyed hash to find it, so a database dump does not hand over class
access (§13.3).

expiresInDays.description:
The code works through 23:59:59 on the day this many days from
today, in the caller's time zone: the profile preference, or
`Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` when there is none or it cannot be read. A code
made at any hour of a day expires at the end of the same day.

maxUses.description:
Defaults to 40 rather than spec §6.1's `null = unlimited`
(O-06). The realistic threat to a bearer code is being
*forwarded*, not guessed, and a use cap is the mitigation
that costs nothing.

**Not nullable on the way in, unlike the stored column.**
A nullable request field cannot express what it promises:
an omitted field and an explicit `null` both arrive as "no
value", so "unlimited" would have been indistinguishable
from "use the default" and one of the two would silently
never happen. A cap of 1000 covers every real cohort, and
the column stays nullable for codes issued before this.

409.description: `CLASS_ARCHIVED` — the class is archived, so it can have no new code.

delete.description:
Revokes without issuing a replacement, and sets `selfJoinEnabled: false`
(§6.4). Both, or neither: a revoked code with self-join still on
advertises a flow that cannot succeed, and a cleared flag without the
revocation leaves a live bearer secret the teacher believes is cancelled.

Idempotent. A class with no active code still returns 204 — "there is no
way in" is the requested state, and reporting failure would invite a
retry that changes nothing.

post.summary: Draft questions from a passage, a transcript or a topic
post.description:
Answers draft questions and writes nothing: the teacher adds the ones
they keep through `createQuestion` or the section writes. Exactly one
source is named: `source`, or `testId` with `stimulusId`, which is a
shared-content passage of the test's draft and which `stimulusId`
resolves only inside that test. Only the source text and the settings
are sent to the provider.

Reserves the call's ceiling before it reaches the provider and settles
what the provider billed after; `usage` says what it cost.

200.description: Draft questions, at most `count` of them, fewer when the provider's answer held some that could not be used.

404.description: No such test or passage in the caller's reach.

post.summary: Look for mistakes in a test's draft
post.description:
Reads the draft's prompts, options, keys, explanations and shared
passages, and answers what is worth a look, hardest first. Nothing is
changed: a one-click `fix` is written by the caller through
`updateQuestion`. No student data and no assignment is sent.

200.description: The findings; empty when nothing is left to look at.

422.description: The draft has no question to check, or holds more than one call reads.

post.summary: Propose a variant of a test
post.description:
Reads the draft's questions, options and keys and proposes rewordings,
reorderings and new wrong options. Answers, points and passages stay
the same. Nothing is saved: the caller copies the test with
`duplicateTest` and applies the changes they keep to the copy's
questions, which sit at the same `number`.

200.description: The proposed changes, in paper order.

422.description: The draft has no question to vary, or holds more than one call reads.

post.summary: Write an explanation for a question's answer
post.description:
Reads the stored question (its prompt, options, key and type) and writes
a short explanation students can read after results are released.
Nothing is saved.

422.description: The question has no answer key to explain.

post.summary: Suggest wrong options for a choice question
post.description:
Reads the stored question's prompt, key and existing options and
suggests up to four wrong options that are not among them. Nothing is
saved.

200.description: One to four suggestions, none of them an option the question already has.

422.description: The question is not a single or multiple choice question, or has no key.

post.summary: Suggest a score for a short answer
post.description:
Reads the question's prompt, type, points and accepted or sample
answers and the student's answer text, and proposes a score and a
comment. The student's name, email, id and class, the attempt's id and
the student's other answers are never sent. The caller must hold
`teaching.grading` as well as `ai.use`, the attempt must be one they
reach as the grading reads do, and their `ai.readStudentAnswers`
preference must be on (`AI_READ_OFF`). The reasons and the comment are
written in the language of the caller's `ai.language` preference. The
AI never writes a mark: a teacher saves one with `gradeAttempt`.

404.description: The attempt, or a question that is not on its paper, is not in the caller's reach.

409.description:
`ATTEMPT_IN_PROGRESS` or `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` — nothing to grade yet, or
nothing that counts.

422.description: The question is not a short answer waiting for a mark by hand (the grader marked this answer itself), or the student left it unanswered.

post.summary: Explain how an assignment's results came out
post.description:
Reads, per question, the correct rate and the eight most frequent wrong
answer texts with their counts, over the papers handed in by the
students the caller reaches, and writes what the class got wrong and
what to do about it. No name, id or attempt is sent, and nothing says
who wrote what. The caller needs `teaching.grading` as well as `ai.use`,
and their `ai.readStudentAnswers` preference must be on
(`AI_READ_OFF`). The text is written in the language of the caller's
`ai.language` preference.

422.description: No paper has been handed in, so there is nothing to explain.

post.summary: Find near-duplicates and untagged questions in your bank
post.description:
Reads the prompts, types and tags of the caller's own questions only,
newest first, at most 2,000 of them, even for a caller who holds
`scope.all`; shared questions are skipped. One request is one bounded
pass of at most five calls to the provider at the same time, inside
about a minute, that reserves its credits once and is charged once.
Tags are suggested for the first 200 questions that have none, 50 to a
call. Duplicates are looked for among all the questions read by
comparing every pair by its words, and one call judges the closest
pairs, at most 20 of them are returned; a rewording that shares few
words with the original is not found. `truncated` is true when the
pass left something undone: the bank held more than it reads or more
untagged questions than it tags, or part of the pass failed or ran out
of time. Apply the suggestions and run it again. Nothing changes until
the caller confirms through the existing writes. Limited to three calls
an hour.

422.description: The caller owns no question to look at.

get.description:
What the caller has used, their allowance, what is left of it and of the
centre's pool, whether they are paused, whether the centre takes
requests for more, their undecided request and the five category sums
the Settings card draws. Reads only: a teacher who has not used AI gets
the allowance a first use would give.

post.summary: Ask for more credits this month
post.description:
One undecided request per teacher per month. Every holder of
`ai.credits.manage` is told. Limited to five calls an hour.

409.description:
`AI_REQUESTS_OFF` — the centre's rule is to pause a teacher who runs
out, so it takes no requests. `AI_REQUEST_PENDING` — the caller's
request this month is undecided.

get.description: Classes the signed-in student belongs to. Backs §9 `/app/classes`.

200.description: The student's own view of each class; never a join code.

post.summary: Enrol with a code, already signed in
post.description:
The already-authenticated half of §6.2 — a student who hits `/join/:code`
while logged in skips straight here. Idempotent when already a member.
Every enrolment is audited with ip and user agent (§6.5).

404.description: Invalid, expired, exhausted or revoked. Same leak rules as `/join/preview`.

413.description: The body is over 8 KiB, which the rate limiter's keys read in full.

get.description: The three §9 sections — **Đến hạn**, **Sắp tới**, **Đã hoàn thành**.

Everything the intro must state before the student starts: duration,
attempts used and allowed, review policy, **the integrity rules in plain
language**, and the audio rules if the test has listening questions
("Mỗi câu nghe được phát tối đa 2 lần") (§9, §10.2).

Announced, visible, never silent — a student is never surprised by a rule
mid-test.

post.summary: Create or resume an attempt
post.description:
Idempotent under a double tap: a partial unique index permits one live
attempt per (assignment, student), so the second insert loses the race
and the handler resumes instead of erroring.

Resuming issues a **new** `sessionId` and records a `resume` event — and
a `session_takeover` event if the previous session was still live. The
superseded session finds out on its next write, via `SESSION_SUPERSEDED`
(§10.1, E2E 7).

`deadlineAt` is computed server-side as
`min(now + durationMinutes, closesAt)` and is authoritative. The client
derives remaining time from it plus the `serverTime` offset, never from
the device clock.

A caller that means to continue a known attempt sends `resume`; a
Continue button must, so that an attempt whose time ran out while the
page was open is not answered with a new one.

resume.description: The attempt the caller means to continue. With it the operation never starts an attempt: when this attempt is no longer the live one it answers `ATTEMPT_CLOSED`.

409.description:
`ATTEMPT_CLOSED` — `resume` named an attempt that is no longer live;
nothing was started.

`ASSIGNMENT_NOT_OPEN` or `ATTEMPT_LIMIT_REACHED`.

`MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULED` — a new attempt would run into a maintenance
window. `details.startsAt` and `details.endsAt` name it. Resuming an
attempt never answers this.

get.description:
**In the student flow, test content is fetched only through here** (§7).

The response contains no `isCorrect`, no `sampleAnswer`, no
`acceptedAnswers` and no `transcript` — at any depth. This is asserted by
a contract test over this file, a Go unit test that walks the live JSON,
and E2E 9 (§13.5, §14). None of those three may be weakened.

A tab that names a session the attempt no longer has is answered with
the paper and `superseded: true`: it may read and may not write, until
the student continues the attempt there (`startOrResumeAttempt`). That
answer replaces no beacon token and records nothing. A tab that names
the attempt's session, or none, is answered as the tab that holds it.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description:
The session this tab holds for the attempt: the `sessionId` of the
last answer it was given by this operation or by
`startOrResumeAttempt`. A tab that holds none sends none.

patch.summary: Autosave answers and flush buffered events
patch.description:
Answers and events land in **one transaction**, so a partial flush cannot
record an event for an answer that was not saved.

Events are inserted `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on
`(attempt, session, clientSeq)`, so a retried batch is a no-op rather
than a failure (D-01).

answers.description: Keyed by the version question's id.

200.description:
Saved. `serverTime` is returned every time so the client's clock
offset self-corrects, and `deadlineAt` is the attempt's deadline as
it stands now, so a teacher's extension or a maintenance window
reaches an open attempt on its next autosave.

409.description:
`SESSION_SUPERSEDED` — opened elsewhere; the client goes read-only
with a plain explanation rather than throwing.
`DEADLINE_PASSED` — the client should submit.
`ATTEMPT_CLOSED` — already submitted or voided.

post.summary: Standalone event flush, including the sendBeacon path
post.description:
Two content types, because `navigator.sendBeacon` cannot set request
headers:

- `application/json` with a normal `Authorization` header, for ordinary flushes.
- `text/plain` carrying `beaconToken` in the body, for the `pagehide`
  flush. `text/plain` is CORS-safelisted, so the request skips preflight —
  necessary, because a preflight on unload is not reliably delivered.

The beacon token grants **append-only event access** and nothing else, so
the weaker credential buys no additional authority.

Fire-and-forget: this is best-effort by design and a failure here must
never block answering or submitting (§10.6).

schema.description:
JSON encoded as text: `{ beaconToken, sessionId, events }`. Sent
as a `Blob` with type `text/plain` from `navigator.sendBeacon`.

202.description: Accepted. Always 202 — the client cannot act on the outcome anyway.

post.summary: Increment the server-authoritative play counter
post.description:
The obvious client-side counter resets on reload, which makes `maxPlays`
meaningless — so the count lives here (§11.4).

**Never rejects a play.** Playback is optimistic: a failed POST does not
block audio, and a student who goes offline to farm replays leaves a gap
in the event log, which is what the integrity timeline is for. Blocking
on a round trip would punish bad wifi far more often than it would catch
anyone.

200.description: `plays` may exceed `maxPlays`. That is reported to the teacher, not enforced.

post.summary: Record one shared listening gesture, deduplicating retries
post.description:
Counts a frozen recording bound to this attempt's version. Every distinct
playId increments its shared counter and appends one server audio_play
event in the same transaction. Retrying the same playId and recording
returns the current count without another increment/event. Reusing a
playId for another recording is PLAY_ID_CONFLICT.

Requires the current writable session, like answer autosave. Playback
remains synchronous and optimistic; no network round trip gates audio.
Counts may exceed maxPlays and never block playback or submission.
Legacy per-question playback uses the existing audio-play endpoint.

200.description: Current server count, including any plays beyond the configured allowance.

409.description: SESSION_SUPERSEDED, ATTEMPT_CLOSED, DEADLINE_PASSED or PLAY_ID_CONFLICT.

post.description:
**Idempotent.** A second call on an already-closed attempt is `409
ATTEMPT_CLOSED`, and a race between a manual tap and an auto-submit
yields one submission.

Objective types are graded immediately; `short_answer` is marked
`requiresManual`. Nothing is rejected based on audio play count (§11.4).

409.description:
`ATTEMPT_CLOSED`.

`DEADLINE_NOT_REACHED` — `reason` was `timer_expired` while the
attempt's deadline is still more than five seconds away, which
happens when the deadline moved after the client last saved.
`details.deadlineAt` is the deadline to wait for; nothing changed.

get.description:
Honours the assignment's review policy. Suppressed fields are **absent**,
not nulled-and-hidden, so no client fallback can surface them.

Question `transcript` and shared-context transcripts appear here only
after submission, gated by each question/recording's own
`showTranscriptAfterSubmit` (§11.3, §13.5). `sampleAnswer` never appears
at all. Material and shared play counts do not depend on score/key flags.

releasesAt.description:
Present only while an `after_close` release is withheld: when
it ends for this student, their effective close. Absent
otherwise.

classAverage.description:
The class average as a percent: the mean, over the students
who qualify, of each one's best graded attempt as earned over
total. Present only when `review.showClassAverage` is on, this
result is released, the assignment has closed, and at least 3
students qualify: a targeted active account with a graded
attempt. Voided, ungraded and unstarted work counts for
nothing. It is an aggregate: no student is named.

sections.description: The paper's parts in test order, as the attempt showed them. The page sums each part's `earned` from the questions whose `sectionId` names it; no review policy hides a part's title or membership.

409.description: `ATTEMPT_IN_PROGRESS` — not yet submitted; `ATTEMPT_VOIDED` — nothing to show.

get.description:
10-minute signature, minted per request (§11.2). A student may only mint
a URL for an asset reachable from an attempt they own — checked against
the version questions, not by asset id alone.

The client fetches this **before** enabling the play button, never inside
the click handler: iOS Safari requires `.play()` to run synchronously in
the gesture, so awaiting anything first would break playback (§11.3).

Cache-Control.description:
`private, max-age=600` (§11.2) — long enough to survive a replay,
short enough that the cache entry cannot outlive the signature it
holds. The TTL and this max-age are the same number on purpose;
they are set from one constant server-side.

get.description:
The caller's own notifications and nobody else's, read or unread,
newest first. A notification first written more than 180 days ago is
deleted, once a day.

Before it reads, the server writes the notifications the passing of
time has earned the caller, at most once in five minutes: an
assignment that opened, a close a day or an hour away, an assignment
about to close with students still to hand in, and a result an
after-close release has made ready. A moment older than seven days is
not made up, and one the caller already holds is left as it is.

Paged by a cursor, not by a page number: ask again with `before` set
to `nextBefore` for the next older page. Ids are time-ordered, so a
notification written while the caller pages never moves a row from one
page to the next.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description:
Only the kinds this console reads (`NotificationAudience`). The
page, `limit` and `nextBefore` count the narrowed list, so a page
is never empty because the other console's rows filled it. Left
out, every kind.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
A notification id, as `nextBefore` gave it: the page holds the
caller's notifications older than it. It is a position in the
caller's own list and never a lookup: an id the caller does not
hold, another user's or nobody's, only bounds the page, which
still holds the caller's rows alone.

200.description: One page. An empty `items` when the caller has none, or none older than `before`.

nextBefore.description: The id of the last item when older notifications exist, else null.

post.summary: Mark the caller's notifications read
post.description:
With `ids`, marks those of the caller's notifications that are unread;
without it, every unread one. A notification already read keeps the
time it was first read.

It marks the caller's own notifications only. An id that is another
user's, already read or not a notification at all is skipped, and the
answer is the same 204 whatever matched, so it tells the caller
nothing about an id that is not theirs.

With `audience`, only that console's kinds are marked, with `ids` or
without: an id of the other console's kind is skipped like any other
id that does not match, and "every unread one" becomes every unread
one of that console. Left out, every kind, as before.

ids.description: Absent means every unread notification the caller has (of `audience`, when it is given).

patch.description:
Merges supplied top-level keys into the caller's stored preferences;
assignmentDefaults replaces that whole nested object. False is a
supplied value and an empty object is a no-op. Null and unknown keys
are refused. Raw request bytes and the normalized merged JSONB object
each have an inclusive 8192-byte cap; exceeding either answers
400 VALIDATION_FAILED after the existing authentication gates.

200.description: The merged persisted preferences, without materialized defaults.

400.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED` — the shape or either byte cap is invalid.

put.description:
Replaces the caller's photo. The file is a PNG or a JPEG of at most
2 MiB, and each side is between 200 and 2048 pixels. The server stores
a 256 x 256 PNG made from the centred square of the upload, so the
original file, its metadata (EXIF, ICC, comments) and its name are
never kept. The response is the whole `CurrentUser`, whose `avatarUrl`
names the new photo; the previous one is deleted.

Checked in this order, each before the next costs anything: the size,
the type from the first bytes (the part's `Content-Type` and the file's
extension are never read), the image header, the dimensions and the
memory the image would need, and only then the decode. At most two
images are decoded at a time across the server. The caller may set a
photo ten times an hour.

The file may be exactly 2 MiB; the request may carry 16 KiB more than
that for the multipart framing, so a file of 2 MiB and one byte is
refused by the size check with `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE`, and a request far
beyond it is cut off before the handler with the same answer.

200.description: Stored. The whole persisted caller, with the new `avatarUrl`.

415.description:
`MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` (not a PNG or a JPEG), `MEDIA_UNREADABLE`
(sniffed correctly but the header or the pixels cannot be read) or
`IMAGE_DIMENSIONS` (a side under 200 or over 2048 pixels, an
image that would need more memory to decode than the server
allows, or a JPEG of more than 32 scans, which a decoder that
cannot be cancelled would spend minutes on). Nothing was stored.

501.description: Object storage is not configured, so no photo can be kept.

delete.description:
Clears the caller's photo and deletes its object, best effort. A caller
with no photo gets the same answer. The response is the whole
`CurrentUser`, without `avatarUrl`.

get.summary: The counts the caller's shell shows
get.description:
How many of the caller's notifications are unread: the dot on the
bell. One count over the caller's own rows, cheap enough to poll. It
writes the caller's due-time notifications first, exactly as
`listNotifications` does, so the count includes them.

`audience` counts one console's kinds only (`NotificationAudience`),
so the student's bell does not light for a teacher kind the same
account holds, nor the reverse. Left out, every kind.

All five switches, whatever the caller's role. One the caller never
saved answers its default: `inApp` true and `email` false.

put.description:
Takes all five switches at once, each event exactly once and in any
order, and stores them for the caller. A client that draws only some
of them sends the others back as it read them.

200.description: Saved. The five switches as stored.

400.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED`: an event is unknown, repeated or missing, or the body is not the five switches.
